views.en: Three questions that are still open
views.zh: 三個還沒有定論的問題
views.lead_en: Each of these is an honest “we are not sure.” The accounts are set side by side, each with its source.
views.lead_zh: 下面每一題，都是老實的「我們還不確定」。說法並列，各自附上出處。

items.topic_en: How are these ancient cultures related to today’s Indigenous peoples?
items.topic_zh: 這些古老的文化，和今天的原住民族是什麼關係？

sides.en: No direct evidence shows that the Peinan Culture seen at archaeological sites was handed down to the present-day Pinuyumayan people.
sides.zh: 「考古遺址所見的卑南文化與現生原住民族群卑南族文化並沒有直接證據顯示兩者之間的傳承關係。」
sides.src: National Museum of Prehistory, “Neolithic” · 史前館〈新石器時代〉

sides.en: The cultures of this period may be related to Indigenous cultures. Snake patterns on pottery and stone show a link between prehistoric and Indigenous cultures, and people often discuss whether they are connected with the origin of Paiwan culture. The same page infers that the Jingpu Culture was left by ancestors of the Amis, and says the Siraya were very likely closely related to the Niaosong Culture.
sides.zh: 「本時期的文化可能與原住民的文化有所關聯。」蛇紋的出現「展露史前文化與原住民文化的連結；常被討論是否為與排灣族文化的起源有關」；「推測靜浦文化是阿美族祖先所留下的文化」；「許多證據都顯示西拉雅族很可能就與蔦松文化有著密切關係」。
sides.src: National Museum of Prehistory, “Iron Age” · 史前館〈鐵器時代〉

sides.en: It may be the ancestral culture of the earliest speakers of Austronesian languages. The museum puts it this way: many scholars think it may be one of their earliest ancestors.
sides.zh: 大坌坑文化「可能是最早的南島語族的祖型文化」。史前館的說法是：「許多學者認為，大坌坑文化是從亞洲東南沿海移入的新文化，並可能是南島語族最早的祖先之一。」
sides.src: Bureau of Cultural Heritage, Dapenkeng site record · 文資局 大坌坑考古遺址

items.note_en: Notice the careful words: “no direct evidence,” “may be,” “people often discuss.” The later the culture, the more links the museum sees; for the older ones it is more cautious. This lesson does not go further than its sources. Each Indigenous people also has its own account of where it came from, and Lesson 3 will listen to those accounts.
items.note_zh: 注意這些小心的字眼：「沒有直接證據」「可能」「常被討論」。越晚的文化，博物館看到的連結越多；對比較早的文化，就比較保留。這一課不會說得比出處更多。每一個原住民族對自己的來歷也有自己的說法，第三課會聽這些說法。

items.topic_zh: 大坌坑文化是什麼時候？

sides.label_zh: 國立臺灣史前文化博物館
sides.en: About 5,500 to 4,200 years ago. (The same page also says these people arrived about 6,000 to 5,000 years ago.)
sides.zh: 「時間大約在距今5,500到4,200年前之間」（同一頁另寫「約距今6,000至5,000年前」這群人來到台灣）。
sides.src: National Museum of Prehistory, “Neolithic” · 史前館〈新石器時代〉

sides.en: About 5,500 to 4,500 years ago.
sides.zh: 「大坌坑文化層（距今約5,500∼4,500年前後）」。
sides.src: Bureau of Cultural Heritage, Dapenkeng site record · 文資局 大坌坑考古遺址

sides.label_en: The Bureau’s records for other sites
sides.en: At Yuanshan, about 6,000 to 5,000 years ago; at Peinan, 5,300 to 4,200; at Fengbitou, about 5,200 to 4,350.
sides.src: Bureau of Cultural Heritage, Yuanshan site record · 文資局 圓山考古遺址

items.note_en: Five sets of numbers for one culture, all from official pages. Part of the reason is simple: a culture does not start and stop at the same moment everywhere, and each site is dated from its own samples. That is why the map uses each site’s own numbers instead of one number for the whole island.
items.note_zh: 同一個文化，五組數字，全都來自官方的頁面。一部分的原因很單純：一個文化不會在每個地方同時開始、同時結束，而每個遺址的年代是用自己的樣本測出來的。所以地圖上用的是每個遺址自己的數字，而不是全島共用一個數字。

items.topic_en: How old are the Wanshan rock carvings?

sides.en: Comparing the carvings with later wood carving and with changes in pattern and style, he estimated that they are about 500 to 1,600 years old.
sides.zh: 發現者「依照露天石刻早於原住民石板屋內木雕，參酌刻紋、圖騰風格變遷，推估岩雕約有500年到1600年歷史」。
sides.src: Bureau of Cultural Heritage, Wanshan site record · 文資局 萬山岩雕群考古遺址

sides.label_zh: 同一份資料的「代表文化層」
sides.en: One view is about 500 years, but the exact age is hard to confirm. The record guesses that the carvings are from the same time as one of two cultures, dated 2,000 to 400 and 2,500 to 1,000 years ago.
sides.zh: 「有一說約距今500年，但詳細年代難以確認，推測與東埔一鄰（2,000∼400年前）或北葉文化層（2,500∼1,000年前）同時期。」
sides.src: Bureau of Cultural Heritage, Wanshan site record · 文資局 萬山岩雕群考古遺址

items.note_en: Lesson 1 said that radiocarbon dating needs something that was once alive, and a line cut into rock is not. The estimate in the record is argued from style. On the map this site is drawn with a dashed ring and never lights up. Saying “we do not know yet” is also an answer.
items.note_zh: 第一課說過，碳十四定年需要「曾經活過的東西」。刻在石頭上的線條不是這樣的東西；資料裡的推估，是從風格去推論的。地圖上這個遺址畫成虛線圈，永遠不會亮。說「我們還不知道」，也是一種答案。

views.rule_en: The rule stays the same as in Lesson 1: views are set side by side, each with its source, and the lesson does not choose.
views.rule_zh: 規則和第一課一樣：說法並列、各附出處，課文不替誰選邊。

phrases.en: Eight sentences for talking about a site
phrases.zh: 談一個遺址的八句英文
phrases.lead_en: These are the sentences a museum label or a guide uses. Tap a speaker to hear each one, then try changing the part in bold.
phrases.lead_zh: 這些是博物館說明牌和導覽員會用的句子。點 🔊 聽每一句，再試著把粗體的部分換掉。

rows.en: Archaeologists have found more than 1,500 slate coffins at the Peinan Site.
rows.html: Archaeologists have found more than 1,500 slate coffins at the Peinan Site.
rows.zh: 考古學家在卑南遺址找到了一千五百多具石板棺。
rows.note_en: have found: the finding is done, and the result still matters now.
rows.note_zh: have found：已經找到了，而且結果到現在還有意義。

rows.en: This layer dates from about 3,500 to 2,300 years ago.
rows.html: This layer dates from about 3,500 to 2,300 years ago.
rows.zh: 這一層的年代大約是 3,500 到 2,300 年前。
rows.note_en: dates from: says how old something is.
rows.note_zh: dates from：說一樣東西的年代。

rows.en: The culture is named after the site where it was first recognized.
rows.html: The culture is named after the site where it was first recognized.
rows.zh: 這個文化是用最早認出它的那個遺址來命名的。
rows.note_en: is named after: where a name comes from.
rows.note_zh: is named after：說一個名字的由來。

rows.en: The jade was brought from more than 100 kilometers away.
rows.html: The jade was brought from more than 100 kilometers away.
rows.zh: 這些玉是從 100 多公里外帶來的。
rows.note_en: was brought from: we know it moved, even if we do not know who carried it.
rows.note_zh: was brought from：知道它被帶過來，即使不知道是誰帶的。

rows.en: By about 1,800 years ago, people here were smelting iron.
rows.html: By about 1,800 years ago, people here were smelting iron.
rows.zh: 到了大約 1,800 年前，這裡的人已經在煉鐵了。
rows.note_en: by + time: at that time or earlier.
rows.note_zh: by＋時間：最晚到那個時候，事情已經發生了。

rows.en: Some scholars think the two figures are hunters.
rows.html: Some scholars think the two figures are hunters.
rows.zh: 有些學者認為，那兩個人是獵人。
rows.note_en: Some scholars think …: one view, not everyone’s.
rows.note_zh: Some scholars think …：這是一種看法，不是所有人的看法。

rows.en: There is no direct evidence that the two are linked.
rows.html: There is no direct evidence that the two are linked.
rows.zh: 沒有直接證據顯示兩者有關聯。
rows.note_en: no direct evidence: it has not been shown. It has not been ruled out either.
rows.note_zh: no direct evidence：還沒有被證明；但也沒有被排除。

rows.en: We still do not know how old the carvings are.
rows.html: We still do not know how old the carvings are.
rows.zh: 我們還不知道這些岩雕有多古老。
rows.note_en: We still do not know …: an honest sentence, and a useful one.
rows.note_zh: We still do not know …：一句老實、也很有用的話。

culture_cards.title_en: A trash heap, a journey of jade, a mountain village, and where to visit
culture_cards.title_zh: 一座垃圾山、玉走過的路、山裡的聚落，以及去哪裡看
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short notes on what these sites show.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 四則短短的說明：這些遺址讓我們看見什麼。

cards.body_en: The Bureau of Cultural Heritage calls Yuanshan the place where the study of Taiwan’s archaeology began, and Taiwan’s largest prehistoric garbage hill. Researchers first recorded the site in 1897. The museum explains that the shell mound is a small hill built up mainly from food waste, with shells, animal bones, fish bones, pottery, and stone tools buried in it. Burials were found in the mound as well, and the Bureau’s record says that for the people of Yuanshan it was more than a place to pile trash: it must have had cultural and social meaning too.
cards.body_zh: 文化資產局說圓山是「台灣考古學研究的濫觴、台灣最大的史前垃圾山」。這個遺址發現於 1897 年。史前館說明，圓山貝塚是以食餘為主的廢棄物所堆積起來的小丘，裡面埋藏大量的貝殼、獸骨、魚骨以及陶片、石器；貝塚中也發現了墓葬；文資局的資料說，貝塚對圓山文化人「不只是堆置垃圾之處，應當也是蘊涵了重要的文化與社會意義」。

cards.body_en: The people of Peinan could get the material for their jade from more than 100 kilometers away, the museum says, and they made many kinds of fine ornaments and tools from it. The same style of earring, with people and an animal, has turned up at other sites in the north and the east.
cards.body_zh: 史前館說，卑南的人能從 100 多公里外的地區取得玉器材料，製作各式各樣精美的裝飾品與工具。同一種人獸形的玉耳飾，在北部和東部的其他遺址也出土過。

cards.en: A village in the high mountains
cards.body_en: At Qubing, on a river terrace in Nantou, an Academia Sinica project uncovered a whole settlement between 1981 and 1987: the remains of houses, 171 slate coffins, and tens of thousands of stone tools and pieces of pottery. The Bureau of Cultural Heritage’s record says the radiocarbon dates show people were living there from about 1,000 to more than 2,700 years ago. The finds do not tell us what these people called themselves.
cards.body_zh: 在南投一處河階上的曲冰，中央研究院的研究計畫在民國 70 到 76 年間挖出一整個聚落：房屋的殘跡、171 座石板棺，以及數以萬計的石器與陶片。文化資產局的資料說，碳十四測定的年代顯示，一千年至二千七百多年前就有人住在這裡。出土的東西沒有告訴我們，這些人怎麼稱呼自己。

cards.zh: 蓋在遺址旁邊的博物館
cards.body_en: The National Museum of Prehistory has three places to visit: its main museum in Taitung City, the Peinan Site Park, also in Taitung City, and the Museum of Archaeology in Tainan. In the north, the Shihsanhang Museum of Archaeology in Bali District, New Taipei City, stands beside the Shihsanhang Site. A site is not a place to dig for souvenirs. Whatever is taken out without being recorded loses its place in the layers, and with it most of what it could have told us.
cards.body_zh: 國立臺灣史前文化博物館有三個地方可以參觀：臺東市的康樂本館、同樣在臺東市的卑南遺址公園，以及臺南的南科考古館。北部的新北市立十三行博物館在八里區，就在十三行遺址旁邊。遺址不是挖紀念品的地方：沒有經過記錄就拿走的東西，會失去它在地層裡的位置——它能告訴我們的事，也跟著失去大半。

myths.myth_en: Stone Age people lived simple, rough lives.
myths.myth_zh: 石器時代的人，過的是簡單粗糙的生活。
myths.fact_en: Between 3,500 and 2,300 years ago the people of Peinan planned their village in rows, carved jade a few millimeters thick, and mended a broken earring so they could go on wearing it.
myths.fact_zh: 距今 3,500 到 2,300 年前，卑南的人把聚落規劃成一排一排的，雕出只有幾公釐厚的玉器，耳飾斷了還修補起來繼續戴。

myths.myth_en: One group of people lived in Taiwan, unchanged, until writing began.
myths.myth_zh: 台灣一直住著同一群人，直到有文字為止都沒有變。
myths.fact_en: The sites show many cultures in different regions. The museum describes people arriving by sea, possibly more than once, and many changes over thousands of years.
myths.fact_zh: 遺址顯示不同的地區有許多不同的文化。博物館的說明裡，有人渡海而來（可能不只一批），幾千年間也有許多變化。

myths.myth_en: Scientists know exactly which of today’s peoples came from each ancient site.
myths.myth_zh: 科學家清楚知道，今天的哪一個族群是從哪一個古老的遺址來的。
myths.fact_en: Not exactly. For the Peinan Culture and the Pinuyumayan people, the museum says there is no direct evidence of a handed-down link. For some later cultures it sees a likely link, and it words each one with care.
myths.fact_zh: 沒有這麼確定。對卑南文化和卑南族，博物館說沒有直接證據顯示傳承關係；對一些比較晚的文化，博物館認為很可能有關聯，但每一句都說得很小心。

myths.myth_en: A dark dot on the map means nobody lived there at that time.
myths.myth_zh: 地圖上的點暗著，就表示那個時候那裡沒有人。
myths.fact_en: It means only that no dated layer from that time has been recorded at that site. People may have lived nearby, or their traces may not have been found yet.
myths.fact_zh: 它只表示那個遺址沒有登錄那個時候的、有年代的文化層。人可能住在附近，或者他們的痕跡還沒被找到。

tricks_head.en: Four things to keep in your pocket

tricks.body_en: Three ages in three words: Paleolithic, Neolithic, Iron Age.
tricks.body_zh: 三個詞記三個時代：舊石器、新石器、鐵器。

tricks.body_en: The oldest layers found so far in Taiwan have stone tools and fire, but no pots.
tricks.body_zh: 目前在台灣找到最古老的地層，有石器和火，但沒有陶罐。

tricks.title_en: A culture is named after a site
tricks.body_en: Dapenkeng, Yuanshan, Peinan, Shihsanhang: each is a place first, then a name for a way of life.
tricks.body_zh: 大坌坑、圓山、卑南、十三行：每一個都先是地名，然後才成了一種生活方式的名字。

tricks.body_en: When the evidence is not enough, say so, and say what would settle it.
tricks.body_zh: 證據不夠的時候就照實說，並且說出還需要什麼才能確定。

notes_head.eyebrow: For Teachers · 給老師的提醒
notes_head.en: Curriculum links, names, and care with sensitive points
notes_head.zh: 課綱對應、名稱，以及幾個需要小心的地方

notes.en: Curriculum links (12-Year Basic Education, social studies). Junior high history content: 歷 Ba-Ⅳ-1 (archaeological excavation and prehistoric cultures); the curriculum’s note suggests discussing a prehistoric site or Indigenous community near the school. Elementary stage 3: Cb-Ⅲ-2 (heritage left in Taiwan by prehistoric, Indigenous, and other cultures).
notes.zh: 課綱對應（十二年國教社會領域）。國中歷史學習內容：歷 Ba-Ⅳ-1「考古發掘與史前文化」；課綱說明建議討論「學校附近的史前遺址或原住民族部落」。國小第三學習階段：Cb-Ⅲ-2。

notes.en: Names. English spellings follow the institutions: Peinan and Pinuyumayan (National Museum of Prehistory; Council of Indigenous Peoples), Shihsanhang (the museum’s own spelling). Other site names are in Hanyu Pinyin; older books in English may use other spellings, such as Tapenkeng. The last age is the Iron Age in the museum’s pages and the Metal Age in the Bureau’s.
notes.zh: 名稱。英文拼法依各機構：Peinan 與 Pinuyumayan（史前館、原住民族委員會）、Shihsanhang（十三行博物館自己的拼法）。其他遺址名用漢語拼音；較早的英文書可能用別的拼法，例如 Tapenkeng。最後一個時代，史前館稱「鐵器時代」，文資局稱「金屬器時代」。

notes.en: On links to present-day peoples, please do not go beyond the sources. The museum’s wording is “no direct evidence” for Peinan and “may be related” for some Iron Age cultures. Students from Indigenous families may know their own community’s account of its origins; that account is evidence of another kind (see Lesson 1), and Lesson 3 takes it up.
notes.zh: 關於和今天各族群的關係，請不要說得比出處更多。博物館對卑南文化的用語是「沒有直接證據」，對鐵器時代一些文化是「可能有所關聯」。原住民族家庭的學生，也許知道自己族群對來歷的說法；那是另一種證據（見第一課），第三課會談。

notes.en: Burials. Much of what we know about Peinan comes from graves. The lesson says so plainly and asks for respect; it shows no human remains. The 3D earring is a simplified sketch, and the map dots mark districts, not exact locations.
notes.zh: 墓葬。我們對卑南的了解，很多來自墓葬。課文照實說明，並請學生帶著敬意；頁面上沒有任何人骨的影像。3D 的玉玦是簡化的示意圖；地圖上的圓點標的是鄉鎮市區，不是確切的位置。

materials.en: The map in this lesson, on a screen or projector
materials.zh: 這一課的地圖（用螢幕或投影機）

materials.en: One index card for each pair of students
A wall or board for the finished cards
materials.zh: 一面可以貼卡片的牆或白板

steps.en: Each pair chooses one of the eight sites and opens its card on the map.
steps.zh: 每兩人選八個遺址裡的一個，在地圖上打開它的卡片。

steps.en: On the index card, write four lines in English: its name, where it is, how old its main layer is, and one thing that was found there.
steps.zh: 在小卡片上用英文寫四行：它的名字、在哪裡、主要那一層有多古老、出土了什麼（寫一樣）。

steps.en: Add one sentence that begins “We still do not know …”
steps.zh: 再加一句用「We still do not know …」開頭的話。

steps.en: Put the cards on the wall from the oldest site to the youngest, and read them aloud in order.
steps.zh: 把卡片從最古老排到最年輕貼在牆上，照順序唸出來。

activities.tip_en: Step 3 is the important one. Students will find that every site has an open question: who the people were, where the jade came from exactly, how old a carving is. Use the History English sentences as models. If a pair chooses Wanshan, ask the class where its card should go in the line, and why that is hard to decide.
activities.tip_zh: 第三步最重要。學生會發現每個遺址都有還沒解開的問題：這些人是誰、玉確切從哪裡來、岩雕有多古老。可以拿「歷史英語」的句子當範本。如果有一組選了萬山岩雕，問問全班：它的卡片該排在隊伍的哪裡？為什麼很難決定？

materials.en: One day of clean, dry classroom waste: paper, wrappers, bottle caps, pencil stubs (nothing wet or sharp)
materials.zh: 教室一天份乾淨、乾燥的回收物與垃圾：紙、包裝、瓶蓋、鉛筆頭（不要濕的或尖銳的東西）

materials.en: Gloves and a large sheet of paper to sort on
materials.zh: 手套，和一大張可以攤開分類的紙

materials.en: A worksheet with three columns: What it is, What it tells us, What it cannot tell us
materials.zh: 一張三欄的學習單：這是什麼／它告訴我們什麼／它不能告訴我們什麼

steps.en: Spread the waste on the paper and sort it into groups, as an archaeologist sorts finds.
steps.zh: 把東西攤在紙上分成幾堆，就像考古學家替出土物分類。

steps.en: Imagine you are an archaeologist 3,000 years from now. What could you say about the people who made this pile?
steps.zh: 想像你是三千年後的考古學家。關於留下這一堆東西的人，你能說出什麼？

steps.en: Now list what you could not know: their names, their language, what they were laughing about.
steps.zh: 再列出你不可能知道的事：他們的名字、說的語言、在笑什麼。

steps.en: Share one sentence with “The evidence suggests that …” and one with “We still do not know …”
steps.zh: 各說一句：一句用「The evidence suggests that …」，一句用「We still do not know …」。

activities.tip_en: This is the Yuanshan shell mound in one class period, with one big difference to point out: the real mound also held burials, so it was more than trash to the people who made it. The third step is the bridge to the reading’s last paragraph: things tell us what people ate and made, and very little about who they said they were. Wash hands afterward, and leave out food waste.
activities.tip_zh: 這是用一節課做一座「圓山貝塚」。有一點很不一樣，要告訴學生：真正的貝塚裡也有墓葬，對當時的人來說，它不只是垃圾堆。第三步接到課文最後一段：東西能告訴我們人們吃什麼、做什麼，卻很少告訴我們「他們說自己是誰」。活動後要洗手；廚餘不要放進來。

links_head.en: Back to the method, and on to the next question
links_head.zh: 回頭看方法，再往下一個問題走

links.en: How Do We Know What Happened Long Ago?
links.zh: 很久以前的事，我們怎麼知道？
links.note_en: Layers, radiocarbon dating, and why dates come as ranges. The made-up pit in that lesson follows the same order as the real sites here.
links.note_zh: 地層、碳十四定年，以及年代為什麼是一個範圍。那一課編出來的探坑，和這一課真實遺址的先後順序是一樣的。

links.note_en: Many peoples and many languages, their own accounts of where they came from, and what scholars say about Taiwan and the Austronesian languages.
links.note_zh: 很多族、很多語言，各族對自己來歷的說法，以及學界怎麼看台灣和南島語族的關係。

lessons.sources_note_en: Facts, dates, and quotations on this page were checked against these sources in October 2026. Quotations keep the spelling and punctuation of the original. Site ages are the Bureau of Cultural Heritage’s unless another source is named
lessons.sources_note_zh: 本頁的事實、年代與引文於 2026 年 10 月依下列資料查證；引文保留原文的寫法與標點。遺址的年代除另外註明外，都依文化資產局

sources.en: The list of 13 National Archaeological Sites (October 2026)
sources.zh: 國定考古遺址共 13 處（2026 年 10 月）：圓山、十三行、大坌坑、鳳鼻頭（中坑門）、卑南、八仙洞、萬山岩雕群、Blihun 漢本、丸山、曲冰、亮島島尾、芝山岩、和平島 B
sources.src: 文化部文化資產局 國家考古遺址出土遺物典藏系統

sources.en: Baxian Caves: layers and ages; representative site of the Changbin Culture
sources.zh: 八仙洞：「代表文化層 距今約30000-15000年（舊石器時代）、6000-4800年（先陶時代）、4700-4500年（新石器時代中期）、3500-2000多年（新石器時代晚期至金屬器時代早期）……」
sources.src: 文資局 八仙洞考古遺址

sources.en: Dapenkeng: name-giving site; layers and ages; “the earliest Neolithic and farming culture, and possibly the ancestral culture of the earliest Austronesian speakers”
sources.zh: 大坌坑：「大坌坑文化命名遺址」；「以大坌坑文化層（距今約5,500∼4,500年前後）為代表……」；「大坌坑文化是台灣最早的新石器時代文化及農耕文化，而且可能是最早的南島語族的祖型文化。」
sources.src: 文資局 大坌坑考古遺址

sources.en: Yuanshan: found in 1897; layers and ages; known for its shell mound
sources.zh: 圓山：「台灣考古學研究的濫觴、台灣最大的史前垃圾山」；「圓山遺址是台灣早期發現的史前遺址之一（1897）」；「以圓山文化層（距今約3,300∼2,300年前）為代表。其他主要有先陶文化、大坌坑文化（距今約6,000∼5,000年前）……」；「貝塚對圓山文化人不只是堆置垃圾之處，應當也是蘊涵了重要的文化與社會意義」；現況：「長久以來遭工程施工嚴重破壞，僅存若干處貝塚及小部分文化層堆積」
sources.src: 文資局 圓山考古遺址

sources.en: Shihsanhang: 1,800 to 500 years ago; furnace and slag; ornaments from outside the island
sources.zh: 十三行：「鐵證如山的金屬器時代、北臺灣現知最早的煉鐵作坊」；「以十三行文化層為代表（距今約1,800∼500年前）」；「出土的煉鐵爐及大量鐵渣顯示已經擁有煉鐵技術」；「出土大量島外物品，如玻璃、黃金、瑪瑙等裝飾物，反映十三行人與外界有頻繁的交易行為」
sources.src: 文資局 十三行考古遺址

sources.en: Peinan: layers and ages; the largest clearly laid-out prehistoric settlement found so far
sources.zh: 卑南：「大坌坑文化（距今5,300 ∼4,200年前）、富山文化（距今4,200∼3,500年前）、卑南文化（距今3,500∼2,300年前）、三和文化（距今2,300∼1,900年前）」；「是目前台灣所發現格局最清楚的史前聚落中最大的一個」；「發掘出土近1,500多具石板棺」
sources.src: 文資局 卑南考古遺址

sources.en: Fengbitou: three cultures in order; the first site to establish the sequence of prehistoric cultures in the south
sources.zh: 鳳鼻頭：「以鳳鼻頭文化層為代表（距今約3,350∼2,450年前），其他主要有大坌坑文化層（距今約5,200∼4,350年前）、牛稠子文化鳳鼻頭類型（距今約4,350∼3,350年前）」；「首先建立南部史前文化層序之遺址」
sources.src: 文資局 鳳鼻頭（中坑門）考古遺址

sources.en: Qubing: excavated 1981–87; 29,000 stone tools, 80,000 pieces of pottery, 171 slate coffins; radiocarbon dates of about 1,000 to more than 2,700 years ago
sources.zh: 曲冰：民國 70 至 76 年三次挖掘，「出土的石器有29000餘件，其中多數為石斧」、「陶質物品八萬餘片」、「石板棺171座」；「經過碳十四測定的年代，曲冰人早在一千年至二千七百多年前即居此地」
sources.src: 文資局 曲冰考古遺址

sources.en: Wanshan rock carvings: 14 rocks at four places; estimates of age
sources.zh: 萬山岩雕群：「共有4處14塊岩石」；「國內唯一的大型岩雕群遺址」；「推估岩雕約有500年到1600年歷史」；「有一說約距今500年，但詳細年代難以確認，推測與東埔一鄰（2,000∼400年前）或北葉文化層（2,500∼1,000年前）同時期。」；「萬山岩雕為原住民原始藝術遺跡」；「依照當地原住民賦予的地名」命名
sources.src: 文資局 萬山岩雕群考古遺址

sources.en: Paleolithic and the Changbin Culture: chipped stone only, no pottery, caves and rock shelters, fire pits, hunting and gathering
sources.zh: 「石器完全以打製的方式製作……也還沒有燒製陶器的技術」；「此遺址大多為岩蔭或洞穴，有發現人類使用的『火塘』遺跡，當時人們以狩獵與採食為生」
sources.src: 國立臺灣史前文化博物館〈臺灣的史前時代：舊石器時代〉

sources.en: Neolithic: arrival by sea about 6,000 to 5,000 years ago with polished stone tools and pottery; the Yuanshan shell mound; the Peinan Culture (planned settlement, more than 2,000 slate coffins, jade from more than 100 km away); no direct evidence of a link with the present-day Pinuyumayan
sources.zh: 「約距今6,000至5,000年前，另一群人由亞洲大陸東南沿海帶入了新石器時代文化……成為最早的航海移民。這些人帶著磨製石器及製作陶器的技術」；圓山貝塚「是以食餘為主的廢棄物所堆積起來的小丘」；「卑南遺址已經出土超過 2,000具的石板棺」；「許多學者認為，大坌坑文化是從亞洲東南沿海移入的新文化，並可能是南島語族最早的祖先之一。目前尚未發現新石器時代舟船的遺留」；先陶文化「到距今6,000年前，島內局部地區仍有人群以狩獵、採集維生，並以打製石器為工具」（見舊石器時代一頁）；「能從100多公里外的地區取得玉器材料」；「考古遺址所見的卑南文化與現生原住民族群卑南族文化並沒有直接證據顯示兩者之間的傳承關係。」
sources.src: 國立臺灣史前文化博物館〈臺灣的史前時代：新石器時代〉

sources.en: Iron Age: ironworking reaches Taiwan about 2,500 years ago; glass and agate beads; cultures of this period may be related to Indigenous cultures; snake patterns and the Paiwan
sources.zh: 「約距今2,500年前，製作鐵器的技術傳入臺灣」；「本時期的文化可能與原住民的文化有所關聯」；蛇紋的出現「展露史前文化與原住民文化的連結；常被討論是否為與排灣族文化的起源有關」；「推測靜浦文化是阿美族祖先所留下的文化」；「許多證據都顯示西拉雅族很可能就與蔦松文化有著密切關係」
sources.src: 國立臺灣史前文化博物館〈臺灣的史前時代：鐵器時代〉

sources.en: The jade earring: museum number, rank, age, material, and size
sources.zh: 人獸形玉玦：典藏號碼 20121600001；級別 國寶；時代 新石器時代卑南文化3500-2300BP；材質 臺灣玉；尺寸 高度70mm、寬40mm、厚度4.5mm、重量15.7g
sources.src: 國立臺灣史前文化博物館 國寶與重要古物

sources.en: The jade earring: description, the two readings by scholars, the mended crack, found in a man’s slate coffin, National Treasure in 2012
sources.zh: 「主要造形是兩個人並肩站立，頭上頂著一隻獸……有學者認為是兩個打獵的人展示獵物……但也有學者認為……好像是獸幻化出人」；「中間有一條斷痕，斷痕兩邊各有一個洞，是修補繼續使用的痕跡」；「大約有兩千多年的歷史」；「在2012年被公告為國寶」
sources.src: 國立臺灣史前文化博物館 語音導覽〈國寶：人獸形玉玦〉

sources.zh: 原住民族的英文名稱（Pinuyumayan、Paiwan、Rukai）

lessons.title: Who Are Taiwan’s Indigenous Peoples?
lessons.blurb_en: Meet the peoples on a map of names, not borders, and slide through the years to watch the government’s official list grow from nine to sixteen, and then take in the Siraya under a new law in 2026. Read each people’s own account of where it came from, and follow the Austronesian languages from Taiwan across two oceans.
lessons.blurb_zh: 在一張「標名字、不標界線」的地圖上認識各族，拖著年份看政府的官方名單從九族變成十六族，再在 2026 年依新的法律加入西拉雅族。讀各族對自己來歷的說法，再跟著南島語言從台灣走過兩個大洋。
lessons.big_idea_en: Taiwan’s Indigenous peoples are many peoples, with many languages and their own accounts of where they came from. The government’s official list has grown over time as peoples asked to be recognized by their own names; the peoples were here long before the list. Their languages belong to the Austronesian family, and many scholars place its homeland in Taiwan, though not all of the evidence agrees.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 台灣的原住民族是很多個民族，有很多種語言，也各有自己對來歷的說法。政府的官方名單隨著各族要求以自己的名字被承認而一再增加；這些民族早在名單出現之前就在這裡了。他們的語言屬於南島語系，許多學者認為南島語言的原鄉在台灣，但證據並不全都一致。

lab.title_en: Names, Not Borders: The Peoples and the Official List
lab.title_zh: 標名字，不標界線：各族與官方名單
lab.how_en: Each name sits near where that people mainly lives, according to the Council of Indigenous Peoples (for the Siraya, the Tainan City Government). Drag the slider, or press a year, to see who was on the government’s official list at that time. Names not yet on the list fade but never disappear. Tap a name to read its card, including the people’s own account of where it came from.
lab.how_zh: 每一個族名，放在原住民族委員會說明的主要分布地區附近（西拉雅族依臺南市政府）。拖動滑桿或按年份，看那個時候政府的官方名單上有哪幾族。還不在名單上的族名會變淡，但不會消失。點一個族名看卡片，卡片上也有那一族自己對來歷的說法。
lab.hello_en: This is 2026: sixteen recognized peoples, plus the Siraya, approved this year under the law on the Pingpu peoples. Drag the slider back to 2000 and forward again to watch the list grow.
lab.hello_zh: 這是 2026 年：十六個法定原住民族，加上今年依平埔原住民族群身分法核定的西拉雅族。把滑桿拖回 2000 年，再往前拖，看名單怎麼一族一族增加。

changes.en: Before 2001 there were nine peoples on the list. The Council’s page on the Thao calls them the tenth people to be recognized, in 2001.
changes.zh: 2001 年以前，名單上有九族。原民會介紹邵族的頁面說，邵族在 2001 年成為第十個被承認的原住民族。

changes.en: 2001: after a long campaign, the Thao were recognized as the tenth Indigenous people, under the name they asked for.
changes.zh: 2001 年：經過長期的爭取，邵族以自己爭取的族名，成為第十個原住民族。
2002 年：噶瑪蘭族被公告認定為原住民族之一。

changes.en: 2004: the Truku were recognized as a separate people.
changes.zh: 2004 年：太魯閣族被公告認定為獨立的民族。
2007 年：撒奇萊雅族成為官方公告承認的原住民族。

changes.en: 2008: the Sediq were recognized as a separate people.
changes.zh: 2008 年：賽德克族被公告認定為獨立的民族。

changes.short_zh: 拉阿魯哇族、卡那卡那富族
changes.en: 2014: on June 26 the government announced the Hla’alua as the 15th people and the Kanakanavu as the 16th.
changes.zh: 2014 年：政府在 6 月 26 日宣布，拉阿魯哇族為第 15 族、卡那卡那富族為第 16 族。

changes.en: 2026: in late July the Executive Yuan approved the Siraya as an Indigenous people, the first under a new law on the status of the Pingpu peoples. Registration opened on August 13, 2026.
changes.zh: 2026 年：7 月底，行政院核定西拉雅族為原住民族，這是《平埔原住民族群身分法》施行後的第一件。族人從 2026 年 8 月 13 日起可以申請登載。

peoples.self_en: They call themselves Pangcah. “Amis,” meaning northerners, is what the Pinuyumayan called the Amis living to their north; scholars then spread the name.
peoples.self_zh: 自稱 Pangcah（邦查）；住在卑南族北邊的阿美族人，被卑南族人稱為「Amis」，有北方人的意思，後來經學術界採用而傳開。
peoples.area_en: The plains east of the Central Mountain Range in Hualien and Taitung, and the Hengchun Peninsula in Pingtung.
peoples.area_zh: 中央山脈以東、立霧溪以南的平原地區，包含花蓮、臺東兩縣，以及屏東縣的恆春半島。
peoples.origin_en: In the north, Amis tradition says the ancestors were born of gods; in the south, that they were born from a stone.
peoples.origin_zh: 北部阿美族人傳說祖先是由神降生而來，南部阿美族人認為祖先是由石頭誕生而來。
peoples.src: Council of Indigenous Peoples · 原住民族委員會

peoples.self_en: Atayal means a person, a true person, or one of us.
peoples.self_zh: atayal 的意思是人、真人或同族人。
peoples.area_en: The mountains of north-central Taiwan, in New Taipei, Taoyuan, Hsinchu, Miaoli, Taichung, Nantou, and Yilan.
peoples.area_zh: 臺灣中北部山區，包含新北市、桃園市、新竹縣、苗栗縣、臺中市、南投縣、宜蘭縣等七縣市。
peoples.origin_en: Long ago a great rock split open, and the first man and woman walked out of it. Their descendants moved to many places and built villages.
peoples.origin_zh: 遠古時代，由大石頭分裂爆開後走出男、女性的祖先，之後遷徙到各地建立部落。
peoples.src: Council of Indigenous Peoples · 原住民族委員會

peoples.area_en: Northwestern Taiwan, on either side of Mount Egongji, in Hsinchu and Miaoli counties.
peoples.area_zh: 臺灣西北部，以鵝公髻山為界分屬於新竹縣與苗栗縣。
peoples.origin_en: A brother and sister survived a great flood and had a child. The pieces of the child were cast into the sea and became the ancestors of the villages and peoples.
peoples.origin_zh: 倖存的兄妹成婚生下小孩，而後將小孩肉、骨、胃、腸分解後投入海中，各別成為各部落與民族的祖先。
peoples.src: Council of Indigenous Peoples · 原住民族委員會

peoples.self_en: Kavalan means people of the plain.
peoples.self_zh: 自稱 kavalan，意思是平原的人類。
peoples.area_en: Zhuangwei and Wujie in Yilan; Xincheng and Fengbin in Hualien; Changbin in Taitung.
peoples.area_zh: 宜蘭縣壯圍鄉、五結鄉；花蓮縣新城鄉、豐濱鄉；臺東縣長濱鄉。
peoples.origin_en: The Kavalan first came from islands to the south, passing a place called Sanasai, and settled on the Lanyang Plain.
peoples.origin_zh: 傳說噶瑪蘭族人最早由南方島嶼，途經地名為 Sanasai 的地方後遷入臺灣，落腳於蘭陽平原。
peoples.src: Council of Indigenous Peoples · 原住民族委員會

peoples.area_en: Xiulin, Wanrong, and Zhuoxi townships in Hualien, and three villages of Ji’an.
peoples.area_zh: 花蓮縣秀林、萬榮、卓溪三鄉，以及吉安鄉慶豐、南華、福興三村。
peoples.origin_en: In prehistoric times the ancestors came by boat from the lands to the south (rowcing, a word for driftwood that here means a boat) and landed on the southwest coast of Taiwan.
peoples.origin_zh: 祖先在史前時代由南洋一帶乘坐 rowcing（漂流木，即船隻之意），在臺灣西南沿海一帶登陸。
peoples.src: Council of Indigenous Peoples · 原住民族委員會

peoples.self_en: Also written Seediq or Sejiq; three groups, Tgdaya, Toda, and Truku. The Truku people of Hualien were recognized as a separate people in 2004, the Sediq in 2008.
peoples.self_zh: 也寫作 Seediq、Sejiq；分為 Tgdaya、Toda、Truku 三群。花蓮的太魯閣族在 2004 年、賽德克族在 2008 年，分別成為獨立的民族。
peoples.area_en: Ren’ai Township in Nantou, and Xiulin and Wanrong in Hualien.
peoples.area_zh: 南投縣仁愛鄉，以及花蓮縣秀林、萬榮兩鄉等地。
peoples.origin_en: The Sediq began in the Central Mountain Range, at a place now called Mudan Rock.
peoples.origin_zh: 發源於中央山脈（Pusu Qhuni），今被稱之為牡丹岩。
peoples.src: Council of Indigenous Peoples · 原住民族委員會

peoples.recognized_zh: 2007 年成為官方承認的原住民族
peoples.area_en: Mainly the Hualien plain, with villages also in the East Rift Valley and along the coast.
peoples.area_zh: 以花蓮平原為主要分布地點，也在花東縱谷、海岸等地建立部落。
peoples.origin_en: The ancestors came from overseas to eastern Taiwan and settled on the Hualien plain.
peoples.origin_zh: 祖先由海外遷入東部後落腳花蓮平原。
peoples.src: Council of Indigenous Peoples · 原住民族委員會

peoples.recognized_zh: 2001 年承認，第十個原住民族
peoples.self_en: Thau, their word for “person”; Japanese scholars took it as the name of the people in the colonial period.
peoples.self_zh: 族名 Thau，源自日本殖民統治時期，日本學者引用邵語稱呼「人」的「Thau」做為邵族的族名。
peoples.area_en: Ita Thau village in Yuchi Township and Dapinglin in Shuili Township, Nantou: around Sun Moon Lake.
peoples.area_zh: 南投縣魚池鄉伊達邵部落和水里鄉大坪林聚落——在日月潭一帶。
peoples.origin_en: The ancestors lived on the Chiayi–Tainan plain. Hunters chased a rare white deer for days into the mountains, until it leapt into Sun Moon Lake.
peoples.origin_zh: 邵族祖先原居於嘉南平原一帶……獵人無意間發現罕見的白鹿……白鹿即躍入日月潭。
peoples.src: Council of Indigenous Peoples · 原住民族委員會

peoples.self_zh: 以 bunun 一詞來稱呼自己。
peoples.area_en: The Central Mountain Range and both sides of it: Nantou, Hualien, Taitung, and Kaohsiung.
peoples.area_zh: 南投縣仁愛鄉、信義鄉，花蓮縣卓溪鄉、萬榮鄉，臺東縣延平鄉、海端鄉，高雄市桃源區、那瑪夏區等地。
peoples.origin_en: The Bunun have several origin accounts. In one of the most widely told, a gourd fell from the sky and split open; a man and a woman walked out of it, and their descendants are the Bunun of today.
peoples.origin_zh: 布農族的起源有好幾種說法。流傳較廣的一種是：有一天從天上掉下了一顆葫蘆，裂開之後，從葫蘆裡走出了一對男女，這一對男女的後裔就是現今的布農族人。
peoples.src: Council of Indigenous Peoples · 原住民族委員會

peoples.self_zh: 以自稱 Tsou 為族名，意思是人。
peoples.area_en: Centered on Alishan in Chiayi, with some in Xinyi, Nantou, and Namasia, Kaohsiung.
peoples.area_zh: 以嘉義縣阿里山鄉為中心，部分在南投縣信義鄉，往南到高雄市那瑪夏區。
peoples.origin_en: The great god Hamo made the Cou from maple leaves, and they moved from Yushan, the Jade Mountain, to where they live now.
peoples.origin_zh: 大神哈默用楓葉創造鄒族人……並從玉山逐漸遷徙到現居地。
peoples.src: Council of Indigenous Peoples · 原住民族委員會

peoples.area_en: Takanuwa and Maya in Namasia District, Kaohsiung; some families were moved to Da’ai Park in Shanlin District after the 2009 typhoon.
peoples.area_zh: 高雄市那瑪夏區的達卡努瓦里、瑪雅里；2009 年莫拉克風災後，有幾戶被安遷至杉林區的「大愛園區」。
peoples.origin_en: A mother named Niun lived alone with her son Parumaci. He kicked a tree: the falling leaves became houses, and with a second kick the leaves became people.
peoples.origin_zh: 一名為 Niun 的母親，與其子 Parumaci 相依為命……一腳踢向……樹幹，樹葉盡落，紛紛相疊，瞬間疊成了一棟棟的房子。再度一踢，落葉悉數成了人。
peoples.src: Council of Indigenous Peoples · 原住民族委員會

peoples.area_en: Gaozhong and Taoyuan in Taoyuan District, and Maya in Namasia District, Kaohsiung.
peoples.area_zh: 高雄市桃源區高中里、桃源里以及那瑪夏區瑪雅里。
peoples.origin_en: The ancestors once lived in the east, at Hlasʉnga, together with little people who kept sacred shells as the home of their first ancestor.
peoples.origin_zh: 族人原居地在東方 Hlasʉnga，曾與矮人共同生活；矮人視「聖貝」為太祖（貝神）居住之所。
peoples.src: Council of Indigenous Peoples · 原住民族委員會

peoples.area_en: Tainan, where the city government counts 50 Siraya communities in 12 districts.
peoples.area_zh: 臺南；臺南市政府說，臺南市仍有 50 處西拉雅族聚落，分布於 12 個行政區。
peoples.note_en: Approved as a Pingpu people under the 2025 law. Registration as a member opened on August 13, 2026; the July 2026 population table has no Siraya column.
peoples.note_zh: 依 2025 年的法律核定為平埔原住民族群。族人從 2026 年 8 月 13 日起可以申請登載民族成員名冊；2026 年 7 月的人口統計表還沒有西拉雅族這一欄。
peoples.src: Council of Indigenous Peoples, July 30, 2026 · 原住民族委員會

peoples.self_en: Ngudradrekai; where the name “Rukai” comes from is still not settled.
peoples.self_zh: Ngudradrekai；「魯凱」這個名稱的來源仍無定論。
peoples.area_en: Both sides of the southern Central Mountain Range, in Kaohsiung, Pingtung, and Taitung.
peoples.area_zh: 中央山脈南段兩側，分屬高雄、屏東與臺東三個行政區。
peoples.origin_en: The three Rukai groups have different accounts. The East Rukai say the ancestors landed from overseas on the east coast; the West Rukai, that the first ancestors were created by the sun, from a clay pot, or from a stone; the Lower Three Villages of Maolin, that the ancestors began around the Big and Small Ghost Lakes.
peoples.origin_zh: 魯凱族三群的說法不同：東魯凱群相傳祖先是由海外登陸東海岸；西魯凱群認為先祖是由太陽、陶壺或石頭創生；高雄茂林下三社的口述歷史，認為祖先是發源在茂林區大、小鬼湖地區。
peoples.src: Council of Indigenous Peoples · 原住民族委員會

peoples.self_en: They call themselves Puyuma; in recent years some have proposed Pinuyumayan for the whole people, to tell it apart from the name of one village.
peoples.self_zh: 自稱 Puyuma；近年有族人提倡以「比努優瑪樣」（Pinuyumayan）作為新的族稱，以區別族稱與部落名。
peoples.area_en: The Taitung plain, around Taitung City and Beinan Township.
peoples.area_zh: 以臺東平原的臺東市、卑南鄉一帶為核心。
peoples.origin_en: There are two accounts: the ancestors were born from bamboo, or from a stone.
peoples.origin_zh: 卑南族的起源有「竹生」、「石生」兩種說法。
peoples.src: Council of Indigenous Peoples · 原住民族委員會

peoples.area_en: From Mount Dawu south to the Hengchun Peninsula, west to Fangliao and east to Taimali, in Pingtung and Taitung.
peoples.area_zh: 北以大武山、南到恆春半島、西到枋寮、東到太麻里及臺東市新園里，包含屏東、臺東兩縣。
peoples.origin_en: In Paiwan tradition, the ancient clay pot is the source from which the ancestors were born. Some Paiwan believe the hundred-pace snake is the ancestor of the traditional leaders.
peoples.origin_zh: 排灣族的文化傳說中，古陶壺是祖先誕生的來源，具有創生的意義。部分排灣族人相信百步蛇是傳統領袖的祖先。
peoples.src: Council of Indigenous Peoples · 原住民族委員會

peoples.self_en: “Yami,” meaning “we,” was first used by the anthropologist Torii Ryūzō in the late 19th century. Some use “Tao,” meaning “person.” The Council says official use is Yami and everyday use is Tao.
peoples.self_zh: 「雅美」是「我們」的意思，由十九世紀末期人類學家鳥居龍藏開始使用；部分族人另外使用「達悟」（tao），意思為「人」。原民會說，官方採用雅美、民間採用達悟。
peoples.origin_en: There are two accounts: the first ancestors came from a stone, or from bamboo.
peoples.origin_zh: 蘭嶼居民的遠祖來源有石生與竹生兩種傳說。
peoples.src: Council of Indigenous Peoples · 原住民族委員會

legend.en: Bright: on the government’s list in the chosen year
legend.zh: 亮著：選定的那一年在政府的名單上

legend.en: Faded: not yet on the list in that year (but the people was there)
legend.zh: 變淡：那一年還不在名單上（但這一族一直都在）

lab.scale_en: Each name is placed near where the Council of Indigenous Peoples says the people mainly lives. The names are not borders, and many people from every group now live in cities all over Taiwan. Population figures are the Council’s for July 2026 (the Ministry of the Interior’s count for the same month is the same total); the Siraya have no figure yet. The nine peoples on the list before 2001 are shown from 2000, because no official page we could find gives the year the first list was made.
lab.scale_zh: 每一個族名，放在原民會說明的主要分布地區附近。族名不是界線；而且每一族都有很多人住在台灣各地的城市。人口數依原民會 2026 年 7 月的統計（和內政部同月的總數相同）；西拉雅族還沒有人口數。2001 年以前在名單上的九族，地圖從 2000 年開始畫，因為我們找不到寫明最早的名單是哪一年訂的官方頁面。
lab.credit_html: Map and code by My Culture Connect. Coastline: Natural Earth 1:10m Land, public domain. No boundaries of any kind are drawn. 地圖與程式由人師教育協會製作；海岸線為公有領域資料，圖上不畫任何界線。

paras: How many Indigenous peoples are there in Taiwan? The answer depends on when you ask. In 2000, the government’s official list had nine peoples. By 2014 it had sixteen. In 2026 the Siraya were approved under a new law for the Pingpu peoples. The peoples themselves did not suddenly appear. They had been here all along, and many of them had to work for years to be recognized by the names they call themselves. So a list made by a government is one kind of record, and like every record, it has a date.

In July 2026 the Ministry of the Interior counted 638,466 Indigenous people in Taiwan, about 2.75 percent of the population. Of these, 7,727 had not yet registered with a particular people. The Amis are the largest people, with more than 238,000 members; the Kanakanavu are among the smallest, with about 500. The Council of Indigenous Peoples counts 42 varieties of Indigenous languages spoken by the sixteen peoples recognized before 2026. Since 2017, the law has called Indigenous languages national languages of Taiwan.

Each people has its own account of where it came from. One Bunun account tells of a gourd that fell from the sky and split open, and a man and a woman walked out. The Atayal tell of a great rock that burst apart. The Cou say the god Hamo made them from maple leaves, and that they later moved from Yushan to where they live now. The Kavalan say their ancestors came from islands to the south. Lesson 1 called these words passed down by mouth. They are evidence of another kind: they tell us how a people understands itself, and they deserve the same respect as any other source.

Names matter, too. In the 1992 constitutional amendments, the government still used the word shanbao, meaning “mountain compatriots.” In 1994 the amendments changed it to yuanzhumin, “original inhabitants,” and in 1997 to yuanzhuminzu, “Indigenous peoples,” a word that recognizes them as peoples. Some names were given by outsiders. The name Yami was first used by a Japanese anthropologist in the late 19th century; some people on Orchid Island also use Tao, which means “person” in their language.

The list keeps changing. In 2001 the Thao were recognized as the tenth people. In 2022 Taiwan’s Constitutional Court ruled that the Indigenous peoples protected by the Constitution include all the Austronesian peoples that already existed in Taiwan, and so the Pingpu peoples as well. A law on the status of the Pingpu peoples followed in 2025, and in July 2026 the Siraya became the first people approved under it. In October 2025 the Council said that nine Pingpu peoples had applied, including the Siraya. Those cases were at different stages.

Taiwan’s Indigenous languages belong to a large family called Austronesian. Encyclopaedia Britannica counts about 1,200 Austronesian languages, spoken from Madagascar, off Africa, to Easter Island in the eastern Pacific. Many linguists think the family began in Taiwan. A 2009 study of language trees placed its origin here about 5,230 years ago. Others have argued that the ancestors of the Polynesians came from farther south, and a 2014 study notes that the genetic evidence is “more controversial” than the evidence from languages. This series sets these views side by side.
paras_zh: 台灣有幾個原住民族？答案要看你什麼時候問。2000 年，政府的官方名單上有九族；到了 2014 年有十六族；2026 年，西拉雅族又依平埔原住民族群的新法律被核定。這些民族不是突然出現的。他們一直都在這裡，而且很多族花了好多年，才讓政府用他們自己的名字承認他們。所以，政府訂的名單是一種記錄；就像每一份記錄一樣，它也有日期。
2026 年 7 月，內政部統計台灣的原住民人口是 638,466 人，大約占總人口的 2.75%；其中 7,727 人尚未申報族別。阿美族是人口最多的一族，超過二十三萬八千人；卡那卡那富族是人口最少的幾族之一，大約五百人。原住民族委員會說，2026 年以前承認的十六族，族語共有 42 種語言別。從 2017 年起，法律明定原住民族語言是台灣的國家語言。
每一族都有自己對來歷的說法。布農族的說法之一是：有一天從天上掉下一顆葫蘆，裂開以後走出一對男女。泰雅族說，一塊大石頭分裂爆開。鄒族說，大神哈默用楓葉創造了他們，後來他們從玉山遷到現在住的地方。噶瑪蘭族說，祖先來自南方的島嶼。第一課把這些叫做「用嘴巴傳下來的話」。它們是另一種證據：告訴我們一個民族怎麼理解自己，也值得和其他史料一樣被尊重。
名稱也很重要。1992 年的憲法增修條文，還用「山胞」這個詞。1994 年改成「原住民」，1997 年再改成「原住民族」——承認他們是一個一個的民族。有些名稱是外人取的。「雅美」這個名稱，是十九世紀末一位日本人類學家開始使用的；蘭嶼也有族人使用「達悟」，在他們的語言裡是「人」的意思。
名單一直在改變。2001 年，邵族成為第十個被承認的民族。2022 年，憲法法庭判決：憲法保障的原住民族，應包括既存於臺灣之所有臺灣南島語系民族——因此也包括平埔族群。2025 年通過了平埔原住民族群身分法；2026 年 7 月，西拉雅族成為依這部法律核定的第一個民族。原民會在 2025 年 10 月說，包括西拉雅族在內，已有九個平埔族群提出申請，各案進度不一。

台灣原住民族的語言屬於一個很大的語系，叫做南島語系。《大英百科全書》說，南島語言大約有 1,200 種，從非洲外海的馬達加斯加，一直分布到東太平洋的復活節島。許多語言學家認為，這個語系起源於台灣。2009 年一份比較語言樹的研究，把它的起源放在大約 5,230 年前的台灣。也有學者主張，波里尼西亞人的祖先來自更南方；2014 年的一份研究則指出，遺傳學的證據比語言的證據「更有爭議」。這個系列把這些看法並列。
questions: Why did the number of peoples on the official list change between 2000 and 2026?
What is the difference between the names Yami and Tao?
Why does this lesson treat each people’s origin account as evidence?
answers: Because peoples asked, often for years, to be recognized by their own names, and because a 2022 court ruling and a 2025 law opened the way for Pingpu peoples. The peoples did not change; the government’s list did.

Yami, meaning “we,” was first used by a Japanese anthropologist in the late 19th century and is still the official name. Tao means “person” in their own language and is a name some people on Orchid Island use.
Because words passed down by mouth are one of the three kinds of evidence from Lesson 1. They show how a people understands itself, so they deserve respect alongside archaeology and written records.

parts.text_en: In 2000 nine names are bright. The faded ones were there too; they were not yet on the government’s list.
parts.text_zh: 2000 年有九個族名亮著。變淡的那些族也都在，只是還不在政府的名單上。

parts.text_en: The Thao of Sun Moon Lake were recognized under the name they asked for. Read their account of the white deer.
parts.text_zh: 日月潭的邵族，以自己爭取的族名被承認。讀一讀他們關於白鹿的說法。

parts.text_en: One name was first used by an outsider; the other means “person” in the people’s own language. The card shows both.
parts.text_zh: 一個名稱是外人開始用的；另一個在族人自己的語言裡是「人」的意思。卡片上兩個都有。

parts.text_en: The Siraya of Tainan were approved in 2026, after a court ruling and a new law. Their card explains why there is no population figure yet.
parts.text_zh: 臺南的西拉雅族在 2026 年核定，在那之前有一個判決和一部新的法律。卡片說明了為什麼還沒有人口數。

lessons.parts_note_en: Now drag the slider slowly from 2000 to 2026 and count the changes. Then ask: what had to happen before each new name could appear?
lessons.parts_note_zh: 現在把滑桿從 2000 年慢慢拖到 2026 年，數一數改變了幾次。再想一想：每一個新的族名出現之前，必須先發生什麼事？

world.lead_en: Austronesian languages are spoken across a vast stretch of sea. Tap a place to see what is spoken there, and how far it is from Taiwan.
world.lead_zh: 南島語言分布在一大片海洋上。點一個地方，看那裡說什麼語言、離台灣有多遠。

places.text_en: Britannica says 14 of the 21 or 22 Austronesian languages once spoken by Taiwan’s Indigenous peoples survive. The Council of Indigenous Peoples counts 42 varieties, counting differently (see Different Views).
places.text_zh: 《大英百科全書》說，台灣原住民族說過的 21 或 22 種南島語言，有 14 種留存至今。原住民族委員會算的是 42 種語言別，算法不同（見「不同的說法」）。

places.text_en: Britannica gives Ilokano, Tagalog, and Cebuano as examples of the Austronesian languages of the Philippines.
places.text_zh: 《大英百科全書》舉伊洛卡諾語、他加祿語、宿霧語，作為菲律賓南島語言的例子。

places.text_en: About 110 Austronesian languages are spoken in Malaysia, Britannica says, mostly in Sabah and Sarawak on the island of Borneo.
places.text_zh: 《大英百科全書》說，馬來西亞大約有 110 種南島語言，大多在婆羅洲的沙巴和砂拉越。

places.text_en: Javanese alone accounts for about one quarter of all speakers of Austronesian languages, according to Britannica.
places.text_zh: 依《大英百科全書》，光是爪哇語，就占所有說南島語言的人大約四分之一。

places.text_en: Off the southeast coast of Africa, the western end of the family. Malagasy is generally regarded as a single language, Britannica says.
places.text_zh: 在非洲東南方外海，是這個語系最西的一端。《大英百科全書》說，馬達加斯加語一般被視為單一的語言。

places.text_en: Hawaiian is one of the Austronesian languages Britannica names among those of the Pacific islands.
places.text_zh: 《大英百科全書》在太平洋島嶼的南島語言中，列出了夏威夷語。

places.text_en: The eastern end of the family, some 2,200 miles west of Chile, Britannica says. From Madagascar to here spans 206 degrees of longitude.
places.text_zh: 這個語系最東的一端，《大英百科全書》說它在智利以西大約 2,200 英里。從馬達加斯加到這裡，橫跨 206 個經度。

world.note_en: The distances are straight-line distances over the globe, worked out on this page from rounded positions, so they are approximate. The map shows only land and sea (Natural Earth, public domain), with no borders. Dots mark a place where an Austronesian language is spoken; they do not show where the speakers came from, and the dashed line only joins two dots: it is not a route anyone sailed.
world.note_zh: 距離是地球上的直線距離（大圓距離），本頁用取整數的位置自己算的，所以是大概的數字。地圖只畫陸地和海（Natural Earth，公有領域），不畫任何界線。圓點標的是說南島語言的地方，不代表說話的人從哪裡來；虛線只是把兩個點連起來，不是誰航行過的路線。

when.eyebrow: On the Timeline · 在時間軸上
when.lead_en: This lesson reaches back to the beginnings of the Austronesian languages and forward to 2026, past the year this series usually stops, because the official list is still changing.
when.lead_zh: 這一課往回講到南島語言的起源，往後講到 2026 年——超過這個系列平常寫到的年份，因為官方名單到現在還在改變。

focus.en: This lesson: from the first Austronesian speakers to today
focus.zh: 這一課：從最早說南島語言的人到今天

when.note_en: This series normally stops in 1996. Lesson 3 goes further on purpose: the official list of peoples changed in 2001, 2002, 2004, 2007, 2008, 2014, and 2026, and a lesson that stopped in 1996 would give a number that is no longer true.
when.note_zh: 這個系列平常寫到 1996 年為止。第三課是刻意寫得更晚：官方名單在 2001、2002、2004、2007、2008、2014、2026 年都改變過，停在 1996 年的話，給出的數字就已經不對了。

sort.lead_en: Eight statements from this lesson. Is each one a people’s own account, a scholar’s finding, or a government decision? There is no timer; the game only counts how many you place correctly on the first try.
sort.lead_zh: 這一課裡的八句話。每一句是某一族自己的說法、學者的研究，還是政府的決定？這裡不計時；遊戲只記下你第一次就分對幾句。
sort.nudge_en: Not that one. Ask: who said this, and how do they know?
sort.nudge_zh: 不是這一種。想一想：這是誰說的？他們怎麼知道？
sort.aria: Choose the kind of statement · 選出是哪一種說法

items.en: A gourd fell from the sky, and a man and a woman walked out of it.
items.zh: 天上掉下一顆葫蘆，裡面走出一對男女。
items.why_en: This is one of several Bunun accounts, as the Council records it.
items.why_zh: 這是布農族好幾種說法中的一種，由原民會記錄下來。

items.en: Hunters chased a white deer until it leapt into Sun Moon Lake.
items.zh: 獵人追著一隻白鹿，直到牠躍入日月潭。
items.why_en: This is the Thao account of how they came to the lake.
items.why_zh: 這是邵族說明自己怎麼來到日月潭的說法。

items.en: The ancestors came from islands to the south, by way of Sanasai.
items.zh: 祖先從南方的島嶼經過 Sanasai 而來。
items.why_en: This is the Kavalan account, as the Council records it.
items.why_zh: 這是噶瑪蘭族的說法，由原民會記錄下來。

items.en: Language trees place the Austronesian origin in Taiwan about 5,230 years ago.
items.zh: 語言樹的研究，把南島語言的起源放在大約 5,230 年前的台灣。
items.why_en: This comes from a 2009 study in the journal Science that built a family tree of 400 languages.
items.why_zh: 這來自 2009 年發表在《Science》期刊、替 400 種語言建立家族樹的研究。

items.en: The genetic evidence is more controversial than the evidence from languages.
items.zh: 遺傳學的證據，比語言的證據更有爭議。
items.why_en: This is from a 2014 study that compared the DNA of an ancient skeleton found on Liangdao with living peoples.
items.why_zh: 這來自 2014 年一份論文，比較亮島出土的古代人骨和現代族群的 DNA。

items.en: The Indigenous peoples protected by the Constitution include all Austronesian peoples that already existed in Taiwan.
items.zh: 憲法保障的原住民族，應包括既存於臺灣之所有臺灣南島語系民族。
items.why_en: This is from the Constitutional Court’s 2022 ruling.
items.why_zh: 這是 2022 年憲法法庭的判決。

items.en: The Thao are the tenth Indigenous people.
items.zh: 邵族是第十個原住民族。
items.why_en: This was the government’s decision in 2001, after the Thao asked for it for a long time.
items.why_zh: 這是政府在 2001 年的決定——在邵族長期爭取之後。

items.zh: 原住民族語言為國家語言。
items.why_en: This is Article 1 of the Indigenous Languages Development Act of 2017.
items.why_zh: 這是 2017 年《原住民族語言發展法》的第一條。

sort.done_en: Three accounts in a people’s own telling, two findings by scholars, and three government decisions. Each kind answers a different question: who we are, what the evidence shows, and what the state recognizes.
sort.done_zh: 三則族人自己的說法、兩項學者的研究、三個政府的決定。每一種回答的問題不一樣：我們是誰、證據顯示什麼、國家承認什麼。
sort.note_en: None of the three kinds is the “real” one. A government list can lag behind a people’s own sense of itself, and a scholar’s finding can be revised. Reading well means knowing which kind of statement you are looking at.
sort.note_zh: 三種說法沒有哪一種才是「真的」。政府的名單可能落在族人自我認同的後面，學者的研究也可能被修正。會讀資料，就是知道自己正在讀的是哪一種說法。

how_we_know.eyebrow: How Do We Know? · 我們怎麼知道？
how_we_know.lead_en: Each of these is a public record you can open yourself.
how_we_know.lead_zh: 下面每一項，都是你自己打得開的公開紀錄。

items.text_en: The origin accounts, names, and places on each card are those the Council of Indigenous Peoples publishes on its page for each people.
items.text_zh: 卡片上的起源說法、族名與分布地區，依原住民族委員會為每一族寫的介紹頁。
items.where_k: Where it lives · 保存在哪裡
items.where_en: Above all in each people’s own memory, language, and ceremonies; written summaries are on the Council’s website.
items.where_zh: 最重要的是在每一族自己的記憶、語言與祭儀裡；文字的摘要在原民會的網站上。
items.src: Council of Indigenous Peoples, “The 16 Indigenous Peoples” · 原民會〈原住民族16族簡介〉

items.text_en: 638,466 Indigenous people, about 2.75 percent of 23,235,002 people in Taiwan. The Council’s table by people gives the same total.
items.text_zh: 原住民人口 638,466 人，占總人口 23,235,002 人的 2.75%。原民會按族別的統計表，總數相同。
items.where_k: Where it is kept · 收藏在哪裡
items.where_en: The household registration records of the Ministry of the Interior, published each month.
items.where_zh: 內政部戶政司的戶籍資料，每個月公布。
items.src: Ministry of the Interior, Department of Household Registration, July 2026 · 內政部戶政司

items.zh: 憲法法庭 111 年憲判字第 17 號判決（2022）
items.text_en: The court ruled that the Indigenous peoples protected by the Constitution include all the Austronesian peoples that already existed in Taiwan, and that other Austronesian peoples whose languages, customs, and traditions still survive, whose members keep their identity, and whose history is on record may apply to be recognized. It gave the government three years to change the law. In the hearing, the Council had argued that the Pingpu peoples were not included.
items.text_zh: 判決說，憲法保障的原住民族，應包括既存於臺灣之所有臺灣南島語系民族，；語言、習俗、傳統等文化特徵至今仍然存續、成員仍維持族群認同、且有客觀歷史紀錄可稽的其他臺灣南島語系民族，均得依其民族意願申請核定為原住民族；並要求在三年內修法或另訂特別法。言詞辯論時，原民會的主張是平埔族群不在其內。
items.where_k: Where to read it · 去哪裡讀
items.where_en: On the Constitutional Court’s website, in Chinese with an English summary.
items.where_zh: 憲法法庭網站，有中文全文與英文摘要。
items.src: Constitutional Court, R.O.C. (Taiwan) · 憲法法庭

items.text_en: A 2009 study of language trees (Gray, Drummond, and Greenhill, in Science) and a 2014 study of ancient DNA (Ko and others, in the American Journal of Human Genetics), with a 2001 article that argues the other way.
items.text_zh: 2009 年比較語言樹的研究（Gray、Drummond、Greenhill，《Science》）、2014 年研究古代 DNA 的論文（Ko 等人，《American Journal of Human Genetics》），以及 2001 年一篇持不同看法的文章。
items.where_k: Where to read it · 去哪裡讀
items.where_en: Summaries are free on PubMed, the U.S. National Library of Medicine’s index; see Sources.
items.where_zh: 摘要可以在美國國家醫學圖書館的 PubMed 免費讀到；見資料出處。

views.en: Three questions with more than one answer
views.zh: 三個不只一種答案的問題
views.lead_en: Each answer below has a source. The lesson does not choose.
views.lead_zh: 下面每一個答案都有出處。課文不替誰選邊。

items.topic_en: Where did the Austronesian languages begin?

sides.en: “[T]he language trees place the Austronesian origin in Taiwan approximately 5230 years ago”
sides.zh: 這份研究的語言樹，把南島語言的起源放在大約 5,230 年前的台灣。
sides.src: Gray, Drummond & Greenhill, Science (2009), PubMed abstract

sides.en: Of the “out of Taiwan” model, “popularly known as the ‘express train to Polynesia’,” they wrote that “it is becoming clear that there is, in fact, little supporting evidence,” and that the immediate genetic substrate of the Polynesian expansion came “not from Taiwan, but from east of the Wallace line.”
sides.zh: 他們說，俗稱「到波里尼西亞的快車」的「出台灣」模型，「越來越清楚的是，其實支持的證據很少」；波里尼西亞人擴張的直接遺傳基礎「不是來自台灣，而是華萊士線以東」。
sides.src: Oppenheimer & Richards, Science Progress (2001), PubMed abstract

sides.label_en: A study of ancient DNA that supports a Taiwan origin (2014)
sides.label_zh: 支持起源於台灣的古代 DNA 研究（2014）
sides.en: “A Taiwan origin … is well supported by linguistic and archaeological evidence. However, human genetic evidence is more controversial.”
sides.zh: 起源於台灣的看法，有語言學與考古學證據的充分支持；但人類遺傳學的證據比較有爭議。
sides.src: Ko et al., American Journal of Human Genetics (2014)

items.note_en: Official pages do not all speak the same way, either. A 2010 page of the Council of Indigenous Peoples says plainly that Taiwan is the common origin of the Austronesian languages 5,000 years ago; a 2003 newsletter of the National Museum of Prehistory lays out several competing models and ends by saying a final answer is still to come. Notice also that each people has its own account of where it came from (see the cards on the map). Those accounts answer a different question, and this lesson does not test them against the scientific studies.
items.note_zh: 官方的頁面說法也不完全一樣。原民會 2010 年的一頁直接寫「臺灣……係5,000年前南島語言之共同起源」；史前館 2003 年的電子報則列出好幾種互相競爭的模型，最後說還要更多研究，「才可對於南島語族起源提出最終的答案」。也請注意：每一族對自己的來歷都有自己的說法（見地圖上的卡片）。那些說法回答的是另一個問題，這一課不拿它們去和科學研究比對真假。

items.topic_en: How many Indigenous languages are there?
items.topic_zh: 台灣有幾種原住民族語言？

sides.en: Taiwan’s Indigenous languages have 42 varieties among 16 peoples.
sides.zh: 「臺灣原住民族語言具 16 族 42 種語言別」。
sides.src: Council of Indigenous Peoples, 2024 language program (PDF) · 原民會 113 年度族語推動計畫

sides.en: “Fourteen of the 21 or 22 Austronesian languages spoken by the pre-Chinese aboriginal population of Taiwan (also called Formosa) survive.”
sides.zh: 台灣原住民族說過的 21 或 22 種南島語言當中，有 14 種留存至今。
sides.src: Encyclopaedia Britannica, “Austronesian languages”

items.note_en: These numbers do not contradict each other so much as count different things. The Council counts language varieties within each recognized people (its 2024 plan gives 42); Britannica counts languages, including ones no longer spoken. Britannica lists Siraya among the languages no longer spoken, while the Tainan City Government describes classes and books to revive it. Telling a language from a dialect is itself a choice that linguists make in different ways.
items.note_zh: 這兩組數字與其說互相矛盾，不如說算的東西不一樣。原民會算的是每一個法定民族裡的「語言別」（它 2024 年的計畫寫的是 42 種）；《大英百科全書》算的是語言，也包括已經沒有人說的。《大英百科全書》把西拉雅語列為已經沒有人說的語言，臺南市政府則說明了族語教師研習、出版繪本與教材等復育的工作。什麼算一種語言、什麼算方言，本身就是語言學家用不同方法做的選擇。

items.topic_en: What should a people be called?
items.topic_zh: 一個民族應該怎麼稱呼？

sides.en: The name Yami was first used by the anthropologist Torii Ryūzō in the late 19th century; some people use Tao. Studies and reports use Yami (official) and Tao (everyday).
sides.zh: 「雅美」一詞「由十九世紀末期人類學家鳥居龍藏開始使用」；「部分族人在族群名稱上也另外使用『達悟』」；研究與報導「分別出現官方採用雅美、民間採用達悟這兩種不同的族稱」。
sides.src: Council of Indigenous Peoples, Yami page · 原民會 雅美族

sides.en: The people’s self-name Puyuma is also the name of one village, so in recent years some have proposed Pinuyumayan for the whole people. The Council’s English pages use Pinuyumayan.
sides.zh: 族人的自稱 Puyuma 也是南王部落的名稱；為了避免混用，「近年有族人提倡以『比努優瑪樣』（Pinuyumayan）來作為卑南族新的族稱」。原民會的英文頁使用 Pinuyumayan。
sides.src: Council of Indigenous Peoples, Pinuyumayan page · 原民會 卑南族

items.note_en: Both examples come from the same official source, which itself records both names. The safest habit is the one the Council follows: give the official name and the name people use, and say who uses which.
items.note_zh: 兩個例子都來自同一個官方出處，而它自己就把兩個名稱都記下來了。最穩當的習慣就是原民會的做法：寫出官方的名稱，也寫出族人用的名稱，並說明誰用哪一個。

views.rule_en: The rule is the same in every lesson: views are set side by side, each with its source, and the lesson does not choose.
views.rule_zh: 每一課的規則都一樣：說法並列、各附出處，課文不替誰選邊。

phrases.en: Eight sentences for talking about peoples and names
phrases.zh: 談民族與名稱的八句英文
phrases.lead_en: Some of these report what a people says about itself; others report what a law or a study says. Tap a speaker to hear each one, then try changing the part in bold.
phrases.lead_zh: 有幾句轉述的是一個民族對自己的說法；有幾句轉述的是法律或研究怎麼說。點 🔊 聽每一句，再試著把粗體的部分換掉。

rows.en: The Bunun tell of a gourd that fell from the sky.
rows.html: The Bunun tell of a gourd that fell from the sky.
rows.zh: 布農族的說法裡，有一顆從天上掉下來的葫蘆。
rows.note_en: tell of: to report a people’s own account without judging it.
rows.note_zh: tell of：轉述一個民族自己的說法，不加評斷。

rows.en: According to Atayal tradition, the first ancestors came out of a rock.
rows.html: According to Atayal tradition, the first ancestors came out of a rock.
rows.zh: 依照泰雅族的傳說，最早的祖先是從石頭裡走出來的。
rows.note_en: According to … tradition: says whose account it is.
rows.note_zh: According to … tradition：說明這是誰的說法。

rows.en: Some Yami people call themselves Tao, which means person.
rows.html: Some Yami people call themselves Tao, which means person.
rows.zh: 有些雅美族人自稱達悟，意思是「人」。
rows.note_en: call themselves: the name a people uses for itself.
rows.note_zh: call themselves：一個民族對自己的稱呼。

rows.en: The Thao were recognized as the tenth Indigenous people in 2001.
rows.html: The Thao were recognized as the tenth Indigenous people in 2001.
rows.zh: 邵族在 2001 年被承認為第十個原住民族。
rows.note_en: were recognized as: a decision made by a government.
rows.note_zh: were recognized as：政府所做的決定。

rows.en: Indigenous people make up about 2.75 percent of Taiwan’s population.
rows.html: Indigenous people make up about 2.75 percent of Taiwan’s population.
rows.zh: 原住民大約占台灣人口的 2.75%。
rows.note_en: make up: to be a part of a whole.
rows.note_zh: make up：構成整體的一部分。

rows.en: Since 2017, Indigenous languages have been national languages of Taiwan.
rows.html: Since 2017, Indigenous languages have been national languages of Taiwan.
rows.zh: 從 2017 年起，原住民族語言就是台灣的國家語言。
rows.note_en: since + year, with have been: true from then until now.
rows.note_zh: since＋年份，配 have been：從那時到現在都是。

rows.en: Austronesian languages are spoken from Madagascar to Easter Island.
rows.html: Austronesian languages are spoken from Madagascar to Easter Island.
rows.zh: 從馬達加斯加到復活節島，都有人說南島語言。
rows.note_en: are spoken from … to …: the range where a language is used.
rows.note_zh: are spoken from … to …：說明一種語言使用的範圍。

rows.en: Many linguists think the family began in Taiwan, but the genetic evidence is debated.
rows.html: Many linguists think the family began in Taiwan, but the genetic evidence is debated.
rows.zh: 許多語言學家認為這個語系起源於台灣，但遺傳學的證據還有爭論。
rows.note_en: is debated: careful people do not yet agree.
rows.note_zh: is debated：認真的人們還沒有共識。

culture_cards.title_en: A changed word, a lake, a national language, and the Pingpu peoples
culture_cards.title_zh: 一個改掉的詞、一座湖、一種國家語言，以及平埔族群
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short notes on names and recognition.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 四則關於名稱與承認的短短說明。

cards.body_en: The constitutional amendments of 1992 spoke of protecting the status of shanbao, “mountain compatriots.” The amendments of 1994 changed the word to yuanzhumin, “original inhabitants.” Those of 1997 changed it again, to yuanzhuminzu, “Indigenous peoples,” and added that the state would act “according to the will of the peoples.” Three amendments in five years, and each word says something different about who is being named.
cards.body_zh: 1992 年的憲法增修條文寫的是保障「山胞」的地位。1994 年的增修條文把這個詞改成「原住民」。1997 年再改成「原住民族」，並加上國家應「依民族意願」保障其地位。五年之內改了三次，每一個詞，對被稱呼的人說的都不一樣。

cards.en: The Thao and Sun Moon Lake
cards.body_en: Sun Moon Lake is one of Taiwan’s best-known sights. In Thao tradition, their ancestors came there following a white deer. The Thao were once classified as part of the Cou, though the two differ greatly in language, religion, and customs; they campaigned to be called by their own name, and in 2001 they became the tenth people on the list. Fewer than 1,000 Thao were counted in July 2026.
cards.body_zh: 日月潭是台灣最有名的景點之一。在邵族的傳說裡，祖先是追著一隻白鹿來到這裡的。邵族在民族分類上曾經被歸類為鄒族，但兩族在語言、宗教、生命禮俗上有很大的差異；他們爭取以自己的名字被稱呼，2001 年成為名單上的第十族。2026 年 7 月統計的邵族人口不到 1,000 人。

cards.body_en: Article 1 of the Indigenous Languages Development Act of 2017 begins: “Indigenous languages are national languages.” The Council of Indigenous Peoples counts 42 language varieties among the 16 peoples recognized before 2026. The National Languages Development Act of 2019 defines national languages as the natural languages used by each of Taiwan’s original groups, together with Taiwan Sign Language.
cards.body_zh: 2017 年《原住民族語言發展法》第一條開頭就說：「原住民族語言為國家語言」。原民會說，2026 年以前承認的十六族共有 42 種語言別。《國家語言發展法》則把國家語言定義為「臺灣各固有族群使用之自然語言及臺灣手語」。

cards.en: The newest people on the list
cards.body_en: Pingpu, “of the plains,” is a name for a group of peoples, each with its own name, such as the Siraya. In 2022 the Constitutional Court ruled that they, too, are among the Indigenous peoples the Constitution protects. A law followed in 2025, and in July 2026 the Siraya of Tainan became the first people approved under it; the Council’s pages give both July 30 and July 31 for the approval. In October 2025 the Council said eight other Pingpu peoples had also applied.
cards.body_zh: 「平埔」是平原的意思，指的是一群民族；每一族都有自己的名字，例如西拉雅族。2022 年，憲法法庭判決他們也屬於憲法保障的原住民族。2025 年通過了相關的法律；2026 年 7 月，臺南的西拉雅族成為依這部法律核定的第一個民族——原民會的頁面上，核定的日期一處寫 7 月 30 日、一處寫 7 月 31 日。原民會在 2025 年 10 月說，另外還有八個平埔族群也已經提出申請。

myths.myth_en: Taiwan’s Indigenous people are one group with one language.
myths.myth_zh: 台灣的原住民是同一群人，說同一種語言。
myths.fact_en: They are many peoples: sixteen recognized peoples, plus the Siraya approved in 2026 under the Pingpu law. The Council counts 42 language varieties among the sixteen.
myths.fact_zh: 他們是很多個民族：十六個法定原住民族，加上 2026 年依平埔族群的法律核定的西拉雅族。原民會說，那十六族共有 42 種語言別。

myths.myth_en: The number of peoples is fixed.
myths.myth_zh: 原住民族的數目是固定的。
myths.fact_en: The government’s list changed seven times between 2001 and 2026, and more Pingpu peoples have applied. The list is a record with a date.
myths.fact_zh: 政府的名單在 2001 到 2026 年之間改變了七次，還有更多平埔族群提出申請。名單是一份有日期的記錄。

myths.myth_en: Indigenous peoples all live in the mountains.
myths.fact_en: The Amis live mainly on the eastern plains, the Kavalan named themselves “people of the plain,” the Yami live on an island, and the Siraya live in Tainan.
myths.fact_zh: 阿美族主要住在東部的平原，噶瑪蘭族的族名就是「平原的人」，雅美族住在島上，西拉雅族住在臺南。

myths.myth_en: Origin stories are just fairy tales.
myths.fact_en: They are a people’s own account, passed down by mouth for generations: evidence of how a people understands itself. They answer a different question from archaeology, not a lesser one.
myths.fact_zh: 它們是一個民族自己的說法，口耳相傳了好幾代——是這個民族怎麼理解自己的證據。它們回答的問題和考古學不一樣，但並不比較不重要。

tricks_head.en: Four things to keep in your pocket

tricks.body_zh: 說「原住民族」，英文用複數 peoples。

tricks.body_en: When you give a number, say which year it is from.
tricks.body_zh: 說出一個數字的時候，也說出它是哪一年的。

tricks.body_en: Give the official name and the self-name, and say who uses which.
tricks.body_zh: 寫出官方的名稱和自稱，並說明誰用哪一個。

tricks.body_en: Report an origin account with “they tell of,” not with “they believe a silly story.”
tricks.body_zh: 轉述起源說法用「他們的說法是……」，不要說「他們相信一個奇怪的故事」。

notes_head.eyebrow: For Teachers · 給老師的提醒
notes_head.en: Curriculum links, a deliberate exception, and care with names
notes_head.zh: 課綱對應、一個刻意的例外，以及名稱上的小心

notes.en: Curriculum links (12-Year Basic Education, social studies). Junior high history content: 歷 Ba-Ⅳ-2 (migrations and traditions of Taiwan’s Indigenous peoples); the curriculum’s note suggests discussing the migration of Austronesian peoples and the distribution of Indigenous peoples, and uses “Indigenous peoples” in a wide sense that includes the Pingpu peoples. Elementary stage 3: Cb-Ⅲ-2.
notes.zh: 課綱對應（十二年國教社會領域）。國中歷史學習內容：歷 Ba-Ⅳ-2「臺灣原住民族的遷徙與傳說」；課綱說明建議討論「南島語族的遷徙與原住民族的分布」，而且這裡的「原住民族」範圍包含平埔族群。國小第三學習階段：Cb-Ⅲ-2。

notes.en: A deliberate exception. This series stops in 1996, but this lesson includes the changes to the official list up to 2026, because a lesson that stopped earlier would give a number that is no longer true. If the list changes again, this lesson will be updated.
notes.zh: 一個刻意的例外。這個系列寫到 1996 年為止，但這一課把官方名單到 2026 年為止的變動都寫進來，因為停在更早的話，給出的數字已經不對了。名單如果再改變，這一課會跟著更新。

notes.en: Names. English names follow the Council of Indigenous Peoples’ English pages: Pinuyumayan, Cou (also written Tsou), Sediq, Hla’alua, Kanakanavu. For Yami and Tao, the Council itself notes both names; the lesson gives both. Please say “Indigenous peoples” (原住民族), not older terms, except when quoting history.
notes.zh: 名稱。英文族名依原民會英文頁：Pinuyumayan、Cou（也寫作 Tsou）、Sediq、Hla’alua、Kanakanavu。雅美與達悟，原民會自己就並列兩個名稱，課文也兩個都寫。請說「原住民族」，不用舊的稱呼，除非是在引用歷史文件。

notes.en: Students from Indigenous families. Some students may know their own people’s account better than any web page. Invite them to share if they wish, and never ask a student to speak for a whole people. Origin accounts in this lesson are short summaries from the Council and are not complete versions.
notes.zh: 原住民族家庭的學生。有些學生對自己族群的說法，可能比任何網頁都清楚。歡迎他們自願分享，但不要要求一位學生代表整個民族發言。本課的起源說法是原民會網站上的簡短摘要，不是完整的版本。

materials.en: An index card for each student

steps.en: On one side, write the name your family calls you, and what it means or why it was chosen, if you know.
steps.zh: 在一面寫下家人叫你的名字，以及它的意思或為什麼取這個名字（如果你知道的話）。

steps.en: On the other side, write a name someone outside your family once gave you, such as a nickname or an English name.
steps.zh: 在另一面寫下家人以外的人給你取過的名字，例如綽號或英文名字。

steps.en: In pairs, explain which name you prefer, and why.
steps.zh: 兩人一組，說說你比較喜歡哪一個名字，為什麼。

steps.en: As a class, connect this to the lesson: why might a people want to be called by its own name?
steps.zh: 全班一起把它連到這一課：為什麼一個民族會希望用自己的名字被稱呼？

activities.tip_en: Keep the focus on the students’ own names; do not ask students to guess or use other people’s ethnic names. The point is to feel why a self-name matters before reading the Yami and Tao card again.
activities.tip_zh: 焦點放在學生自己的名字；不要請學生去猜或使用別人的族名。重點是先體會「自己的名字」為什麼重要，再回頭讀雅美與達悟那張卡。

materials.en: A large sheet of paper or the board

steps.en: Each student writes on a sticky note one language spoken in their home, even a few words of it.
steps.zh: 每位同學在便利貼上寫下家裡說的一種語言，就算只會幾個詞也可以。

steps.en: Group the notes on the board. Count how many languages the class has together.
steps.zh: 把便利貼在白板上分組，數一數全班一共有幾種語言。

steps.en: Read Article 3 of the National Languages Development Act together: national languages are the natural languages used by each of Taiwan’s original groups, and Taiwan Sign Language.
steps.zh: 一起讀《國家語言發展法》第三條：國家語言是臺灣各固有族群使用之自然語言及臺灣手語。

steps.en: Discuss: what helps a language stay alive in a family?
steps.zh: 討論：什麼能讓一種語言在家裡繼續活下去？

activities.tip_en: No student should feel pressed to name a language they would rather not. Students who speak an Indigenous language may be invited, never required, to teach the class a greeting.
activities.tip_zh: 不要讓任何學生覺得必須說出自己不想說的語言。會說族語的學生可以邀請、但絕不要求，教全班一句問候。

lessons.title: How Did the World First Draw Taiwan?
lessons.blurb_en: Page through five old maps from libraries and a museum, from 1584 to 1849. Watch the island change from uncertain islands to the shape we know, read what mapmakers admitted they did not know, and see how historians still disagree about where the name Formosa came from.
lessons.blurb_zh: 翻看五張來自圖書館和博物館的老地圖，從 1584 年到 1849 年。看這座島怎麼從幾座不確定的島，變成我們熟悉的形狀；讀一讀畫地圖的人承認自己不知道的地方；再看看歷史學者對「福爾摩沙」這個名字從哪裡來，到現在還意見不同。
lessons.big_idea_en: Old maps show what their makers knew, and what they did not. Mapmakers far away drew Taiwan split in two, too thin, or blank in places before they drew it close to today’s shape. All that time, Indigenous peoples were living across the island. The maps are evidence about the people who made them, as much as about the island.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 老地圖讓我們看見畫地圖的人知道什麼，也看見他們不知道什麼。遠方的地圖師曾經把台灣畫成兩座島、畫得太瘦、留下空白，後來才畫得接近今天的形狀。這段時間裡，原住民族一直住在島上各地。這些地圖是關於畫圖者的證據，也是關於這座島的證據。

lab.title_zh: 五張地圖，從 1584 年到 1849 年
lab.how_en: Each image is a real map from a library or museum that openly licenses its images. Press Newer or tap a year to change maps; the timeline beside it moves too. Tap a numbered dot to read what it marks, and zoom in to read the old labels. Today’s coastline sits beside the map, not on top of it, because the old shapes do not fit and that is the point.
lab.how_zh: 每一張都是真的老地圖，來自明確開放影像授權的圖書館或博物館。按「較晚」或點年份換一張，旁邊的時間軸也會跟著動。點有編號的圓點，看它標的是什麼；放大可以讀老地圖上的字。今天的海岸線放在旁邊對照，不疊在上面，因為老地圖的形狀對不上，而這正是要看的地方。
lab.hello_en: Five maps, from 1584 to 1849. Press Newer, or tap a year, and watch the island change shape. Tap a numbered dot to read what it marks.
lab.hello_zh: 五張地圖，從 1584 年到 1849 年。按「較晚」或點一個年份，看這座島的形狀怎麼改變。點有編號的圓點，看它標的是什麼。

maps.year_label_zh: 1584 年（1579 年畫成；這一份印於 1608 年）
maps.maker_en: Ludovico Georgio, a Portuguese mapmaker, first drew this map in 1579; it appeared in the 1584 edition of Abraham Ortelius’s atlas, engraved by Frans Hogenberg. This copy comes from the 1608 Italian edition, printed in Antwerp by Jan Baptista Vrients.
maps.maker_zh: 葡萄牙地圖師 Ludovico Georgio 在 1579 年畫成，1584 年收進 Abraham Ortelius 的地圖集，由 Frans Hogenberg 雕版。這一份出自 1608 年在安特衛普由 Jan Baptista Vrients 印行的義大利文版。
maps.notice_en: West is at the top (OCCIDENS), so north is on the right and the coast of China runs along the bottom. Off that coast are “Lequeio parua” and “Ins. Fermosa,” and farther along, “Lequeio magna.” The historian Paul Kua reads the first two as Taiwan drawn as two islands, and Lequeio magna as Okinawa, drawn much too large.
maps.notice_zh: 西方在上面（OCCIDENS），所以北方在右邊，中國的海岸線橫在下方。海岸外是「Lequeio parua」和「Ins. Fermosa」，再過去是「Lequeio magna」。歷史學者 Paul Kua 認為，前兩座是把台灣畫成了兩座島，Lequeio magna 則是畫得太大的沖繩。
maps.held_en: David Rumsey Map Collection, Stanford Libraries
maps.held_zh: David Rumsey 地圖典藏（史丹佛大學圖書館）
maps.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 · David Rumsey Map Collection, David Rumsey Map Center, Stanford Libraries · trimmed to the map’s frame
maps.say_en: 1584: west is at the top. Find Ins. Fermosa, low on the left.
maps.say_zh: 1584 年：西方在上面。在左下方找「Ins. Fermosa」。

hots.en: OCCIDENS means west. On this map, west is at the top, east (ORIENS) is at the bottom, and north is on the right.
hots.zh: OCCIDENS 是「西」。這張地圖西方在上面、東方（ORIENS）在下面，北方在右邊。

hots.en: “Ins. Fermosa”: Ins. is short for insula, Latin for island, and Fermosa is an old spelling of Formosa. Kua reads this island as the north of Taiwan.
hots.zh: 「Ins. Fermosa」：Ins. 是拉丁文 insula（島）的縮寫，Fermosa 是 Formosa 的舊拼法。Kua 認為這座島是台灣的北部。

hots.en: “Lequeio parua”: little Lequeio. Parua (parva) is Latin for small. Kua reads it, with Ins. Fermosa, as Taiwan split into two islands.
hots.zh: 「Lequeio parua」：小 Lequeio。parua（parva）是拉丁文的「小」。Kua 認為它和 Ins. Fermosa 合起來，是被拆成兩座島的台灣。

hots.en: “Lequeio magna”: great Lequeio. Magna is Latin for great. Kua reads it as Okinawa, drawn much too large.
hots.zh: 「Lequeio magna」：大 Lequeio。magna 是拉丁文的「大」。Kua 認為這是畫得太大的沖繩。

hots.en: IAPAN (split on the sheet as IA … PAN): Japan. It sits below the coast of China, because on this map east is at the bottom.
hots.zh: IAPAN（圖上拆成 IA … PAN 兩段）：日本。它畫在中國海岸的下方，因為這張地圖東方在下面。

maps.en: A Chart of the Coast of China from Cambodia to Nanquam with Part of Japan
maps.zh: 從柬埔寨到 Nanquam 的中國海岸圖（含日本的一部分）
maps.maker_en: Credited to Edmond Halley, John Senex, and Nathaniel Cutler, in Atlas Maritimus & Commercialis, printed in London in 1728 for James and John Knapton and other booksellers.
maps.maker_zh: 作者記為 Edmond Halley（哈雷）、John Senex、Nathaniel Cutler，收在 1728 年於倫敦為 James 與 John Knapton 等書商印行的《Atlas Maritimus & Commercialis》（航海與商業地圖集）。
maps.notice_en: A chart for sailors: straight lines spread out from compass roses so that a navigator could follow one compass direction from place to place. Taiwan, labeled “I Formosa,” is long and much too thin. A few names are written on the island, among them “Toywan,” which looks like the early spellings of Taiwan in this lesson; more names are written in the sea just east of it.
maps.notice_zh: 這是給航海的人用的海圖：直線從羅盤玫瑰向四面八方畫出去，讓航海的人可以沿著一個羅盤方向，從一個地方航向另一個地方。台灣標成「I Formosa」，又長又太瘦。島上寫了幾個地名，其中一個是「Toywan」，看起來很像這一課裡台灣的早期拼法；島的東邊海上還寫著別的地名。
maps.held_en: David Rumsey Map Collection, Stanford Libraries
maps.held_zh: David Rumsey 地圖典藏（史丹佛大學圖書館）
maps.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 · David Rumsey Map Collection, David Rumsey Map Center, Stanford Libraries · trimmed to the map’s frame
maps.say_en: 1728: a chart for sailors. Taiwan is there, but much too thin.
maps.say_zh: 1728 年：給航海的人用的海圖。台灣在上面，但是畫得太瘦了。

hots.en: “I Formosa”: the island is drawn long and narrow. Names written on it include Parconta, Wanken, Toywan, and Tonha.
hots.zh: 「I Formosa」：這座島畫得又長又窄。島上寫的地名有 Parconta、Wanken、Toywan、Tonha。

hots.en: “Pescadore Is.”: the Pescadores. Pescadores means fishermen in Portuguese and Spanish. Today these are the Penghu Islands.
hots.zh: 「Pescadore Is.」：Pescadores，葡萄牙文和西班牙文的「漁夫」。就是今天的澎湖群島。

hots.en: A compass rose. The straight lines spreading from it are rhumb lines: follow one and you keep the same compass direction.
hots.zh: 一個羅盤玫瑰。從它畫出去的直線叫恆向線：沿著一條走，羅盤的方向就一直不變。

hots.en: IAPAN: Japan, at the top right. On this chart north is at the top.
hots.zh: IAPAN：日本，在右上角。這張海圖北方在上面。

hots.en: “La Philipina Ilands”: the Philippines, to the south.
hots.zh: 「La Philipina Ilands」：菲律賓，在南邊。

maps.en: General Map of China (the area around Taiwan)
maps.zh: 中國全圖（台灣附近的部分）
maps.maker_en: Jean Baptiste Bourguignon d’Anville, geographer to the King of France, in his Nouvel atlas de la Chine, published in The Hague by Henri Scheurleer in 1737.
maps.maker_zh: 法國國王的地理學家 Jean Baptiste Bourguignon d’Anville，收在 1737 年由 Henri Scheurleer 在海牙出版的《中國新地圖集》（Nouvel atlas de la Chine）。
maps.notice_en: The title says the map was drawn from maps that the Kangxi Emperor (Cang-Hi) had Jesuit missionaries make on the spot. The island is labeled “Taiouan ou Isle Formose”: Taiouan, or Formosa Island. The same name, “Tai-ouan,” also marks a place on the west coast. The west coast is crowded with names; the east coast has almost none.
maps.notice_zh: 地圖的標題說，它是根據康熙皇帝（Cang-Hi）派耶穌會傳教士實地測繪的地圖畫成的。島上寫著「Taiouan ou Isle Formose」：Taiouan，也就是福爾摩沙島。同一個名字「Tai-ouan」也標在西海岸的一個地方。西海岸擠滿了地名，東海岸幾乎一個也沒有。
maps.held_en: David Rumsey Map Collection, Stanford Libraries
maps.held_zh: David Rumsey 地圖典藏（史丹佛大學圖書館）
maps.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 · David Rumsey Map Collection, David Rumsey Map Center, Stanford Libraries · cropped to the area around Taiwan
maps.say_en: 1737: the shape is much closer to today’s. Compare the two coasts.
maps.say_zh: 1737 年：形狀跟今天接近多了。比一比東西兩邊的海岸。

hots.en: “Taiouan ou Isle Formose”: two names for the whole island, joined by ou, French for or.
hots.zh: 「Taiouan ou Isle Formose」：整座島的兩個名字，中間的 ou 是法文的「或」。

hots.en: “Tai-ouan”: here the same name also marks a place on the west coast.
hots.zh: 「Tai-ouan」：同一個名字，在這裡也標在西海岸的一個地方。

hots.en: “Isles de Pong-hou ou de Pescadores”: the Penghu Islands, given two names.
hots.zh: 「Isles de Pong-hou ou de Pescadores」：澎湖群島，給了兩個名字。

hots.en: The west coast: one place name after another.
hots.zh: 西海岸：一個地名接著一個地名。

hots.en: The east coast: almost no names at all.
hots.zh: 東海岸：幾乎沒有地名。

maps.en: Map of the Island of Formosa and the Coasts of China
maps.zh: 福爾摩沙島與中國沿岸圖
maps.maker_en: Jacques Nicolas Bellin, engineer of the French navy, in his Petit Atlas Maritime (volume 3, no. 59), Paris, 1764.
maps.maker_zh: 法國海軍工程師 Jacques Nicolas Bellin，收在 1764 年於巴黎出版的《小海事地圖集》（Petit Atlas Maritime）第三冊第 59 號。
maps.notice_en: The shape is close to today’s. Big letters run up the island: “Tai-ouan ou Isle Formose.” On the west coast, “Tai-ouan ou Taiwan” also marks one place. And Bellin wrote what he did not know onto the map. Across the mountains: “l’Interieur de cette Isle n’est pas connu,” the inside of this island is not known. Along the east: “toute cette Côte est très peu connue,” this whole coast is very little known.
maps.notice_zh: 形狀已經和今天很接近。整座島上用大字寫著「Tai-ouan ou Isle Formose」；西海岸上，「Tai-ouan ou Taiwan」又標了一個地方。而且 Bellin 把自己不知道的事也寫在地圖上：山區寫著「l’Interieur de cette Isle n’est pas connu」（這座島的內部不清楚）；東邊寫著「toute cette Côte est très peu connue」（這一整段海岸所知甚少）。
maps.held_en: David Rumsey Map Collection, Stanford Libraries
maps.held_zh: David Rumsey 地圖典藏（史丹佛大學圖書館）
maps.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 · David Rumsey Map Collection, David Rumsey Map Center, Stanford Libraries · trimmed to the map’s frame
maps.say_en: 1764: the mapmaker wrote down what he did not know. Tap number 6.
maps.say_zh: 1764 年：地圖的作者把自己不知道的事寫了下來。點第 6 號。

hots.en: “Carte de l’Isle Formose”: Map of the Island of Formosa.
hots.zh: 「Carte de l’Isle Formose」：福爾摩沙島地圖。

hots.en: “Is. de Pong-hou ou des Pêcheurs”: the Penghu Islands. Pêcheurs is French for fishermen.
hots.zh: 「Is. de Pong-hou ou des Pêcheurs」：澎湖群島。Pêcheurs 是法文的「漁夫」。

hots.en: “Ft Zelandia ruine”: Fort Zeelandia, in ruins. The Dutch fort is the subject of Lesson 5.
hots.zh: 「Ft Zelandia ruine」：熱蘭遮城，已成廢墟。這座荷蘭人的城是第五課的主題。

hots.en: “Tai-ouan ou Taiwan”: here the name marks one place on the west coast, beside the fort.
hots.zh: 「Tai-ouan ou Taiwan」：在這裡，這個名字標的是西海岸上、城堡旁邊的一個地方。

hots.en: “TAI-OUAN ou ISLE FORMOSE,” in big letters running up the whole island: here the same name is used for the whole island.
hots.zh: 「TAI-OUAN ou ISLE FORMOSE」，大字沿著整座島往上寫：在這裡，同一個名字用在整座島上。

hots.en: “l’Interieur de cette Isle n’est pas connu”: the inside of this island is not known. Not known to the mapmaker: people lived there.
hots.zh: 「l’Interieur de cette Isle n’est pas connu」：這座島的內部不清楚。是畫地圖的人不清楚；那裡是有人住的。

hots.en: “toute cette Côte est très peu connue”: this whole coast is very little known.
hots.zh: 「toute cette Côte est très peu connue」：這一整段海岸所知甚少。

maps.en: Map of the Chinese Coast and of Formosa
maps.zh: 中國沿岸與福爾摩沙圖
maps.maker_en: Compiled by Philipp Franz von Siebold; print by P.C. Tesch after Kampmann. The sheet is marked “Nippon I” and “Tab. III.”
maps.maker_zh: Philipp Franz von Siebold 編繪；P.C. Tesch 依 Kampmann 的底稿製版。圖紙上印著「Nippon I」和「Tab. III」。
maps.notice_en: This 1849 print looks back. Its title says it was compiled from Dutch maps of the seventeenth century, most of them drawn by hand. Its names include “Zelandia,” “Taywan,” and “De Visschers Eilanden of Pehoe,” the Fishermen’s Islands, or Pehoe. The small numbers in the sea are soundings: water depths for sailors.
maps.notice_zh: 這張 1849 年的地圖是在回顧過去：標題說，它是根據十七世紀的荷蘭地圖（大多是手繪的）編成的。圖上的地名有「Zelandia」、「Taywan」，還有「De Visschers Eilanden of Pehoe」（漁夫群島，或 Pehoe）。海上的小數字是給航海的人看的水深。
maps.held_zh: 荷蘭國家博物館（阿姆斯特丹）
maps.say_en: 1849: a newer print of much older Dutch maps. Find Zelandia and Taywan.
maps.say_zh: 1849 年：用更早的荷蘭地圖印成的新地圖。找找 Zelandia 和 Taywan。

hots.en: The title: “Kaart van de Chineesche Kust en van Formosa,” compiled “according to Dutch, mostly hand-drawn, maps of the seventeenth century,” by Siebold, 1849.
hots.zh: 標題：「Kaart van de Chineesche Kust en van Formosa」（中國沿岸與福爾摩沙圖），Siebold 1849 年「依據十七世紀、大多為手繪的荷蘭地圖」編成。

hots.en: “Zelandia” and “Taywan,” side by side on the coast.
hots.zh: 「Zelandia」和「Taywan」，在海岸上並排。

hots.en: “Pehoe,” on the largest of “De Visschers Eilanden,” the Fishermen’s Islands. Visschers is an old Dutch spelling of fishermen.
hots.zh: 「Pehoe」，在「De Visschers Eilanden」（漁夫群島）最大的那座島上。Visschers 是荷蘭文「漁夫」的舊拼法。

hots.en: Soundings: small numbers that give the depth of the water, for sailors.
hots.zh: 水深：海上的小數字，告訴航海的人這裡的水有多深。

hots.en: A compass rose, with lines for sailors spreading from it.
hots.zh: 一個羅盤玫瑰，給航海的人用的線從它畫出去。

legend.en: Numbered dot: something to look at on this map
legend.zh: 有編號的圓點：這張地圖上值得看的地方

legend.en: Today’s coastline, beside the map for comparison
legend.zh: 今天的海岸線，放在旁邊對照

lab.scale_en: The maps are shown as the library or museum published them, only trimmed to the frame; the 1737 map is cropped to the area around Taiwan. The numbered dots were placed by My Culture Connect by looking at the images, and the readings of the old labels are ours; spellings follow the maps. Old maps are not stretched to fit today’s coastline.
lab.scale_zh: 地圖照圖書館或博物館公開的樣子呈現，只裁到圖框；1737 年那張裁成台灣附近的部分。有編號的圓點是人師教育協會看著影像放上去的，老地名的讀法也是我們讀的，拼法照地圖原樣。老地圖沒有被拉扯去對齊今天的海岸線。
