paras: Imagine drawing a map of a place you have only seen from a ship. You can see the coast, but not the mountains behind it, and not the far side. The maps in this lesson were made by outsiders in Europe, and they show the island as those mapmakers knew it. All that time, Indigenous peoples were living across the island, in the mountains, on the plains, and along both coasts. They are not shown on these maps, but they were there.

The oldest map in this lesson is dated 1584. Ludovico Georgio, a Portuguese mapmaker, first drew it in 1579, and it was printed in an atlas by Abraham Ortelius. West is at the top. Off the coast of China are two islands labeled “Lequeio parua” and “Ins. Fermosa.” Ins. is Latin for island, and Fermosa is an old spelling of Formosa. The historian Paul Kua reads the two together as Taiwan, drawn in two pieces.

Formosa means beautiful in Portuguese. A story taught in Taiwan’s textbooks says that Portuguese sailors in the 1500s saw the island and called it Ilha Formosa, “beautiful island.” In 2017, the historian Weng Jiayin and the writer Huang Yan argued that the island those sailors called Formosa was probably Okinawa, and that the Spanish were the first to give the name to Taiwan, in the 1580s. In 2020, Paul Kua answered that Portuguese maps already named Taiwan this way in the 1550s.

In 1728, a sea chart printed in London still drew Taiwan long and much too thin. Nine years later, in 1737, a French geographer named d’Anville published a map that looks much closer to today’s. Its title says it was drawn from maps that the Kangxi Emperor had Jesuit missionaries make on the spot. On that map, the west coast is full of place names, but the east coast is almost empty.

In 1764, Jacques Nicolas Bellin, a mapmaker for the French navy, wrote something honest right on his map. Across the mountains: “the inside of this island is not known.” Along the east coast: “this whole coast is very little known.” The mountains and the east coast were not empty, of course. Indigenous peoples lived there. Those places were unknown to the mapmaker, not empty.

Where does the name Taiwan come from? Victor Mair, a scholar of Chinese languages, writes that it comes from the name of an Indigenous people in the southwest of the island. A Dutch ship’s log from 1622 already spelled the area “Teijoan” and “Taiyowan.” On the maps in this lesson, the name is used in two ways, sometimes on the same map: for the whole island (“Tai-ouan ou Isle Formose”) and for one place on the west coast (“Tai-ouan ou Taiwan,” beside a ruined Dutch fort).
paras_zh: 想像你要畫一張地圖，畫的是一個你只從船上看過的地方。你看得到海岸，卻看不到後面的山，也看不到另一邊。這一課的地圖都是歐洲的外地人畫的，畫的是這座島在他們心中的樣子。這段時間裡，原住民族一直住在島上各地：山區、平原，還有東西兩邊的海岸。這些地圖上看不到他們，但他們就在那裡。

這一課最古老的地圖，年代是 1584 年。它是葡萄牙地圖師 Ludovico Georgio 在 1579 年畫成的，後來收進 Abraham Ortelius 的地圖集印行。這張地圖西方在上面。中國的海岸外有兩座島，分別標著「Lequeio parua」和「Ins. Fermosa」。Ins. 是拉丁文的「島」，Fermosa 是 Formosa 的舊拼法。歷史學者 Paul Kua 認為，這兩座島合起來就是台灣，只是被畫成了兩塊。
Formosa 在葡萄牙文是「美麗的」。台灣的歷史課本教過一個說法：1500 年代的葡萄牙水手看到這座島，叫它 Ilha Formosa，「美麗的島」。2017 年，歷史學者翁佳音和作家黃驗主張，那些水手叫做 Formosa 的島可能是沖繩，第一個把這個名字用在台灣的是西班牙人，時間在 1580 年代。2020 年，Paul Kua 回應說，葡萄牙的地圖在 1550 年代就已經這樣稱呼台灣了。
1728 年，一張在倫敦印的海圖，還是把台灣畫得又長又太瘦。九年後，1737 年，法國地理學家 d’Anville 出版了一張跟今天接近多了的地圖。它的標題說，這張圖是根據康熙皇帝派耶穌會傳教士實地測繪的地圖畫成的。在那張地圖上，西海岸滿滿都是地名，東海岸卻幾乎是空的。
1764 年，替法國海軍畫地圖的 Jacques Nicolas Bellin，直接在地圖上寫了很誠實的話。山區寫著：「這座島的內部不清楚。」東海岸寫著：「這一整段海岸所知甚少。」當然，山區和東海岸並不是空的，原住民族就住在那裡。那些地方只是畫地圖的人不清楚，並不是空無一人。

「台灣」這個名字是從哪裡來的？研究漢語的學者梅維恆（Victor Mair）寫道，它來自島上西南部一個原住民族群的名稱。一份 1622 年的荷蘭航海日誌，已經把那一帶拼成「Teijoan」和「Taiyowan」。在這一課的地圖上，這個名字有兩種用法，有時候就在同一張地圖上：一種是整座島（「Tai-ouan ou Isle Formose」），一種是西海岸上的一個地方（「Tai-ouan ou Taiwan」，旁邊是一座已成廢墟的荷蘭城堡）。
questions: On the 1584 map, which two islands does the historian Paul Kua read as Taiwan?
Bellin wrote that the inside of the island was “not known.” Not known to whom?
On the 1764 map, the name Tai-ouan is used in two ways. What are they?
answers: “Lequeio parua” and “Ins. Fermosa,” the two islands closest to the coast of China. He reads them as Taiwan drawn in two pieces.
To the mapmaker. Indigenous peoples lived in the mountains and along the east coast.
For the whole island (“Tai-ouan ou Isle Formose,” in big letters) and for one place on the west coast (“Tai-ouan ou Taiwan,” beside the fort). The 1737 map does the same.

items.topic_zh: 最早把台灣叫做 Formosa 的是誰？

sides.en: Portuguese sailors passing in the 1500s called the island Formosa for its beautiful scenery. Radio Taiwan International notes that history textbooks taught this.
sides.zh: 央廣的報導寫道：「歷史課本上教過，葡萄牙人16世紀行經台灣時，因美麗的風景稱台灣為福爾摩沙(Formosa)」。
sides.src: Radio Taiwan International (2017)

sides.en: Portuguese sailing records place their Formosa at about 25 degrees north, north of Taipei, so it was probably Okinawa. Most documents call Taiwan “Lequeo pequeno.” The words “As Ilhas Fermosas” appear in a Spanish ship’s log in the 1580s, so the first to call Taiwan by this name were probably the Spanish.
sides.zh: 翁佳音表示，葡萄牙人航海誌裡的 Formosa 都在北緯 25 度，已經在台北以北，應該是沖繩而不是台灣；絕大部分文獻稱台灣本島為 Lequeo pequeno（小琉球）；1580 年代西班牙人的航海誌才出現 As Ilhas Fermosas（美麗諸島），所以第一個稱台灣為 Fermosas 的應該是西班牙人。
sides.src: Radio Taiwan International (2017), reporting their book

sides.en: Kua agrees that “Ilhas Fermosas” in the Spanish navigator Francisco Gali’s 1584 log means Taiwan, but says that to call the Spanish the first is “going too far.” Portuguese maps name the island “Fremosa” in 1554 and “Fermosa” after that, so “it is safe to conclude that the naming of Taiwan as Formosa happened in the early 1550s.”
sides.zh: Kua 同意西班牙航海家 Francisco Gali 1584 年航海日誌裡的「Ilhas Fermosas」指的是台灣，但認為因此說西班牙人是第一個，是「說過頭了」。葡萄牙的地圖在 1554 年就把這座島標成「Fremosa」，之後又寫成「Fermosa」，所以他的結論是：台灣被叫做 Formosa，發生在 1550 年代初期。
sides.src: Kua, Anais de História de Além-Mar 21 (2020)

items.note_en: The two sides read many of the same kinds of documents, sailing directions, maps, and letters, and agree about the Spanish log of 1584. They disagree about the Portuguese records before it.
items.note_zh: 兩方讀的是很多同類的文件（航海指南、地圖、書信），也都同意 1584 年那份西班牙航海日誌指的是台灣；分歧在於更早的葡萄牙紀錄。

culture_cards.title_en: A name that stayed, fishermen in three languages, four directions, and a fort
culture_cards.title_zh: 留下來的名字、三種語言的漁夫、四個方向，和一座城
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short notes on what the old maps left behind.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 四則關於老地圖留下了什麼的短短說明。

cards.body_en: The name Formosa has not disappeared from English. Encyclopaedia Britannica gives the strait to the west of Taiwan two names: the Taiwan, or Formosa, Strait. And Bellin’s 1764 map is titled Carte de l’Isle Formose, Map of the Island of Formosa.
cards.body_zh: Formosa 這個名字並沒有從英文裡消失。《大英百科》給台灣西邊的海峽兩個名字：台灣海峽，或福爾摩沙海峽。Bellin 1764 年的地圖，標題就是 Carte de l’Isle Formose（福爾摩沙島地圖）。

cards.body_en: The maps call the Penghu Islands the Pescadores (Portuguese or Spanish), the Pêcheurs (French), and De Visschers Eilanden (Dutch). All three mean fishermen. Three languages, one meaning.
cards.body_zh: 這些地圖把澎湖群島叫做 Pescadores（葡萄牙文或西班牙文）、Pêcheurs（法文）、De Visschers Eilanden（荷蘭文）。三個都是「漁夫」。三種語言，同一個意思。

cards.body_en: The 1584 map prints the directions in Latin on its four sides: OCCIDENS (west) at the top, ORIENS (east) at the bottom, MERIDIES (south) on the left, and SEPTEMTRIO (north) on the right. Turn the page so that SEPTEMTRIO is at the top, and the map starts to look familiar.
cards.body_zh: 1584 年的地圖在四邊印著拉丁文的方向：上面是 OCCIDENS（西）、下面是 ORIENS（東）、左邊是 MERIDIES（南）、右邊是 SEPTEMTRIO（北）。把紙轉到 SEPTEMTRIO 在上面，這張地圖就開始變得眼熟了。

cards.body_en: In 1764 Bellin marked Fort Zeelandia as a ruin. In 1849 Siebold, compiling from Dutch maps of the 1600s, drew “Zelandia” beside “Taywan.” Who built the fort, and why there? That is the next lesson.
cards.body_zh: 1764 年，Bellin 把熱蘭遮城標成廢墟。1849 年，Siebold 根據 1600 年代的荷蘭地圖編圖，把「Zelandia」畫在「Taywan」旁邊。這座城是誰蓋的、為什麼蓋在那裡？那是下一課的故事。

myths.myth_en: Old maps are useless because they are wrong.
myths.myth_zh: 老地圖畫錯了，所以沒有用。
myths.fact_en: Their mistakes are evidence. A wrong shape or an empty coast shows what the mapmaker knew, and from whom.
myths.fact_zh: 畫錯的地方本身就是證據。形狀不對、海岸空白，讓我們看見畫地圖的人知道什麼、又是從誰那裡知道的。

myths.myth_en: Everyone agrees that Portuguese sailors named Taiwan Formosa.
myths.myth_zh: 大家都同意是葡萄牙水手把台灣取名為 Formosa。
myths.fact_en: That is the story in the textbooks. In 2017 the historian Weng Jiayin and the writer Huang Yan argued that the Spanish were first; in 2020 Paul Kua argued that the Portuguese named Taiwan Formosa in the early 1550s.
myths.fact_zh: 那是課本裡的說法。2017 年歷史學者翁佳音和作家黃驗主張西班牙人才是第一個；2020 年 Paul Kua 則主張葡萄牙人在 1550 年代初期就把台灣叫做 Formosa。

myths.myth_en: The name Taiwan means terrace bay.
myths.myth_zh: 「台灣」這個名字的意思是「臺形的海灣」。
myths.fact_en: That is a surface reading of the two Chinese characters. Victor Mair says the characters were chosen for their sound, and that the name comes from the name of an Indigenous people.
myths.fact_zh: 那只是兩個漢字字面上的意思。梅維恆說，這兩個字是取它們的音，名字本身來自一個原住民族群的名稱。

myths.myth_en: The places marked “not known” were empty.
myths.myth_zh: 地圖上寫著「不清楚」的地方，就是沒有人住。
myths.fact_en: Indigenous peoples lived there. “Not known” describes the mapmaker, not the land.
myths.fact_zh: 原住民族就住在那裡。「不清楚」說的是畫地圖的人，不是那片土地。

tricks_head.en: Four things to keep in your pocket

tricks.body_en: North is not always at the top.

tricks.title_en: Who drew it, and for whom?
tricks.body_en: A sailors’ chart and an atlas map answer different questions.
tricks.body_zh: 海圖和地圖集裡的地圖，要回答的問題不一樣。

tricks.body_en: An empty space on a map is a gap in the mapmaker’s knowledge.
tricks.body_zh: 地圖上的空白，是畫地圖的人知識上的空白。

tricks.body_en: A name on a map shows the name was used, not who gave it.
tricks.body_zh: 地圖上有一個名字，只說明有人用這個名字，不說明是誰取的。

notes.en: Care with words. Please avoid saying that Europeans “discovered” or “opened up” Taiwan; people already lived here. Say that a mapmaker drew, named, or did not know a place.
notes.zh: 用字上的小心。請不要說歐洲人「發現」或「開闢」了台灣；這裡本來就有人住。可以說地圖師畫了、命名了，或不清楚某個地方。

notes.en: The readings of old labels on this page are our own, made by zooming in on the images; old engraved letters can be hard to read. If you or your students read a label differently, open the library’s full image and decide together. Readings of which islands are Taiwan on the 1584 map follow Paul Kua.
notes.zh: 本頁老地圖上的字，是我們放大影像自己讀的；老雕版的字有時不好認。如果你或學生讀出不一樣的字，可以打開圖書館的完整影像，一起判斷。1584 年那張地圖上哪幾座島是台灣，依 Paul Kua 的解讀。

materials.en: A sheet of paper and a pencil for each student
materials.zh: 每人一張紙和一支鉛筆

steps.en: Stand in the classroom doorway and do not walk in. Draw a map of the room using only what you can see from there.
steps.zh: 站在教室門口，不要走進去。只用從那裡看得到的東西，畫一張教室的地圖。

steps.en: Now walk through the room and fix your map with a different color.
steps.zh: 現在走進教室繞一圈，用另一種顏色修正你的地圖。

steps.en: In pairs, compare: which parts were wrong or empty at first, and why?
steps.zh: 兩人一組比一比：哪些地方一開始畫錯或是空白的？為什麼？

steps.en: As a class, connect this to the 1728 and 1764 maps: what could the mapmakers see, and what could they not?
steps.zh: 全班一起把它連到 1728 年和 1764 年的地圖：畫地圖的人看得到什麼？看不到什麼？

activities.tip_en: Ask students to label one empty part of their first map “not known,” the way Bellin did. Then ask: not known to whom?
activities.tip_zh: 請學生像 Bellin 一樣，在第一張地圖的一塊空白上寫「不清楚」，再問：是誰不清楚？

materials.en: The map viewer on this page, on a screen or a projector
materials.zh: 本頁的地圖展示台（用螢幕或投影）

materials.en: A copy of the five questions below for each group
materials.zh: 每組一份下面的五個問題

steps.en: Give each group one of the five maps.
steps.zh: 每一組分到五張地圖中的一張。

steps.en: Answer: Who made it? When? For whom (sailors, readers of an atlas)? Which way is up? What does it say it does not know?
steps.zh: 回答：誰畫的？什麼時候？畫給誰用（航海的人、看地圖集的讀者）？哪邊是上面？它說自己不知道什麼？

steps.en: Find one label on the map and copy it exactly, with the original spelling.
steps.zh: 在地圖上找一個名字，照原本的拼法一字不差地抄下來。

steps.en: Report to the class in English, using one sentence from History English.
steps.zh: 用英文向全班報告，用上一句歷史英語的句子。

activities.tip_en: Each map’s card gives the maker, date, and library record, so groups can check their answers.
activities.tip_zh: 每張地圖的卡片上有作者、年代和館藏紀錄，各組可以自己核對答案。
